detail.title: A robust portfolio selection problem with price impacts in discrete time
detail.abstract: In this paper, we solve a robust portfolio choice problem of an investor with stochastic factors and price impacts in discrete time. Trading incurs both permanent and temporary price impacts and the investor exhibits ambiguity aversion toward the model estimation errors of the asset return and stochastic factor processes. The robust portfolio choice problem is formulated such that the investor aims to maximize the local mean-variance preference on his investment returns and the mark-to-market profits & losses due to price impacts, netting execution costs and penalized by the model estimation errors. Different from the case with temporary price impact only, we show that the investor may not always trade toward the so-called aim portfolio. Compared with the non-robust case, the ambiguityaverse investor adopts a more conservative trading strategy; while the investor tends to trade toward the assets with higher permanent price impacts or lower market resilience rates, with the trading speed constrained by the magnitude of his ambiguity aversion. Our simulation studies indicate that the robust trading strategy generally performs better than the non-robust one, and mark-to-market profits & losses due to permanent price impacts can result in the net Sharpe ratio to be higher than the gross Sharpe ratio.

affiliations: University of South Carolina - Darla Moore School of Business

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to participate in producing the judgment for which fiduciaries are legally responsible. This Article examines that problem in the setting of registered investment advisers' proxy voting under Rule 206(4)-6 and the Advisers Act's fiduciary standard. AI-assisted proxy voting is not merely a new technological tool; in some configurations, AI can gather information, apply voting policies, generate recommendations, explain those recommendations, or cause votes to be cast without individualized human review. The central question is therefore not whether advisers may use AI, but when AI-assisted reliance becomes AI-driven substitution. 
The duties that govern that question are familiar: care, loyalty, retained responsibility, and the recordkeeping and compliance architecture that makes voting decisions reviewable. What AI changes is not the content of those duties but the operational account of how they are satisfied when part of the analytic process has moved into a computational system. 
The Article makes three principal contributions. First, it identifies the fiduciary principle that AI places under pressure: a fiduciary may rely on outside inputs but may not substitute those inputs for its own judgment. Second, it reconceives reviewability as reconstructability, recasting the inquiry from whether the adviser can inspect a model's internal reasoning to whether it can reconstruct the inputs, instructions, policy, output, human review, conflict controls, and records that produced the vote. Third, it offers a four-mode typology of AI use in proxy voting: research assistant, policy-execution tool, recommendation engine, and autonomous or default voter. The typology maps increasing AI participation in voting judgment onto increasingly demanding fiduciary controls. Together, these contributions yield a framework, organized around ex-ante governance, use-stage controls, and ongoing monitoring, for determining when AI-assisted voting remains consistent with fiduciary judgment.

title: What Students Get: AI Failure Modes Across K-12 Subject Areas in Texas, New York, and Mississippi Working Paper -Draft in Progress

detail.title: What Students Get: AI Failure Modes Across K-12 Subject Areas in Texas, New York, and Mississippi Working Paper -Draft in Progress
detail.abstract:
With 86% of students now using AI tools for schoolwork, the gap between AI use and AI literacy has become a structural problem in American education. This paper presents field research testing three commercially available AI systems — Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini — across 30 prompts in chemistry, civic history, and English literature. Test corpora were developed from publicly available curriculum standards in Texas, New York, and Mississippi, with prompts written in realistic student voice and scored on a six-dimension universal rubric supplemented by category-specific dimensions.

The study identifies a clear failure mode gradient: AI performs best on well-defined factual tasks (chemistry, mean 2.82–2.96 per dimension), worse on contested historical narratives (civic history, 2.81–2.96), and worst on literary interpretation (literature, 2.54–2.85). Model rankings reverse across domains, and hallucination clusters in specialized disciplinary vocabulary where students are least equipped to detect it. The paper argues that the dominant "cheating" framing misidentifies a literacy problem as a behavioral one, and contributes both empirical evidence of subject-specific failure modes and a replicable evaluation framework that educators can apply without technical expertise.

title: Data Mining for Retail Product Recommendation using Data Analysis

detail.title: Data Mining for Retail Product Recommendation using Data Analysis
detail.abstract: This research paper focuses on the use of data mining techniques to develop product recommendation systems in retail environments. By analyzing customer transaction data and purchasing behavior, the study identifies patterns and relationships between products. Using techniques such as Association Rule Mining, Clustering, and Classification, the research aims to improve recommendation accuracy and customer satisfaction. The findings help retailers optimize sales strategies, enhance user experience, and improve decision-making. The study also incorporates recommendation algorithms, including collaborative filtering and content-based filtering, to generate personalized product suggestions. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) is performed to understand the dataset and extract meaningful insights. The performance of the recommendation system is evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and support-confidence measures. The results indicate that data mining significantly improves the relevance and efficiency of product recommendations, leading to increased customer satisfaction, better decision-making, and higher sales.

title: Generational views on accounting: A case study on Gen Z

detail.title: Generational views on accounting: A case study on Gen Z

publicationDetails.journalName: ESCP Business School Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: As questions are being raised in the field of accounting about the role it plays within environmental initiatives, intergenerational perspectives, including the values that underpin them, remain largely absent from the development of accounting standard-setting processes and principles. Gen Z is becoming increasingly visible in sustainability debates, assuming 'emerging' leadership roles in shaping broader societal discussions, while living with many nuances that raise important questions about their views of accounting principles. Drawing on qualitative vignette-based interviews, we explore how members of Gen Z make sense of 'traditional' accounting principles (e.g., quantification, objectivity, expertise) and 'alternative' approaches characterized by narratives, emotions, and nonexpert perspectives in the context of a sustainability project. Our findings indicate a pronounced openness toward socially oriented forms of 'alternative' accounting, often grounded in participants' lived experiences and socio-political contexts. However, this openness coexists with persistent attachments to numbers, professional expertise, and claims of objectivity. We also observe intragenerational tensions around engagement and contested values. This study highlights the importance of incorporating generational perspectives into debates on the future of accounting, particularly in relation to sustainability, to address declining student interest in accounting and reflect on its emancipatory potential in the context of current social and environmental crises.

title: Documentary Credit and Documentary Collection in Export Trade: Traditional Practices and the Role of Artificial Intelligence

detail.abstract:
This paper explains the concept of Documentary Credit (Letter of Credit) and Documentary Collection used in international trade finance. It discusses their meaning, types, working procedures, parties involved, and key documents required in export-import transactions. The study also compares Documentary Credit and Documentary Collection on the basis of risk, security, cost, and suitability in international business.

Special emphasis has been given to the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern trade finance. The paper highlights practical applications of AI such as automated document verification, fraud detection, sanctions screening, predictive risk analysis, and digital trade finance platforms. AI technologies including OCR, machine learning, blockchain integration, and NLP are transforming traditional paper-based systems into faster, more secure, and efficient processes.

The study concludes that while traditional trade finance instruments remain essential for international trade, AI is significantly improving accuracy, reducing processing time, and minimizing operational risks in export-import transactions.

detail.abstract:
This doctoral research investigates the impact of operational management style on employee performance within facility management organizations in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA). The study addresses a critical gap in the literature by focusing on leadership and management practices in technical, high-risk, and performance-driven operational environments. Given the strategic importance of facility management in supporting infrastructure reliability, safety, and service quality under Saudi Vision 2030, understanding the relationship between management behavior and workforce performance is essential.

A quantitative research design was employed using a structured questionnaire distributed to 400 employees across facility management organizations in Saudi Arabia. The study examined the influence of five management styles—transformational, democratic, transactional, laissez-faire, and authoritarian—on employee performance indicators such as work quality, teamwork, punctuality, innovation, and safety compliance. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, reliability testing, correlation analysis, and regression modeling.

The findings demonstrate that transformational and democratic management styles have the strongest positive effects on employee performance, while transactional management provides moderate benefits in structured operational contexts. Conversely, laissez-faire and authoritarian approaches showed limited or negative influence on morale, communication, and long-term productivity. The study contributes empirical evidence to management theory while offering practical recommendations for leadership development in the Saudi facility management sector.

detail.abstract: This paper focuses on how Pakistan has mediated in the long-standing strategic rivalry between the United States and Iran, a conflict of nuclear competition, coercive sanctions, and structural mistrust. The study is based on the mediation theory and the middle-power diplomacy, which implies a qualitative case study approach based on secondary data from academic literature, policy reports, and geopolitical developments occurring between 2015 and 2026. The analysis concludes that the role of Pakistan is more of a facilitative one, focused on maintaining backchannel communication and facilitating short-term de-escalation and not structural conflict resolution. The instrumental performance of Pakistan depends on the relational positioning, which allows it to act as a channel of indirect participation in the highly limited diplomatic space. Yet its influence is limited by the structural asymmetries, conflicting regional interests, and the lack of political determination among the major players. The mediation of Pakistan, therefore, is indicative of a greater change in international relations, where middle powers play a role in conflict management by informal and situational, as opposed to formal, negotiation networks. The work fills a literature gap on the topic of third-party mediation in the relations between the USA and Iran, which helps comprehend how the emergent actors can overcome the intricate geopolitical disputes.

title: THE ASCENT READINESS GAP: Why the Manager-to-Leader-of-Leaders Transition Fails

detail.title: THE ASCENT READINESS GAP: Why the Manager-to-Leader-of-Leaders Transition Fails

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the founder of BlackRidge Institute and developer of the Leadership Readiness Diagnostic and the Four Leadership Transitions framework. BlackRidge Systems, LLC is a commercial entity that markets and licenses these instruments. This interest is disclosed in accordance with standard academic transparency practices.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the ASCENT readiness gap, the point at which proven first-line managers are promoted into leader-of-leaders roles without adequate preparation for the systems-level, indirect, and developmental demands the transition requires. Drawing on peer-reviewed research in leadership development, organizational psychology, and transition theory, combined with longitudinal practitioner observation across operational environments, the paper argues that first-line management success often predicts ASCENT transition risk rather than transition success, that post-promotion development is structurally insufficient at the leader-of-leaders level, and that a diagnostic-first approach to readiness assessment can materially change outcomes. Existing research consistently identifies recurring failure patterns at the manager-to-leader-of-leaders transition, including direct-execution persistence, systems-thinking deficits, manager-development avoidance, and misalignment between first-line management identity and senior leadership role demands. These dimensions are typically addressed in isolation by existing programs. This paper integrates these findings and positions ASCENT failure not as a generic capability gap but as a readiness failure, a predictable and assessable condition that precedes promotion rather than follows it. The paper introduces the Leadership Readiness Diagnostic (LRD) at the ASCENT level, a developmentfocused, behaviorally anchored instrument designed to evaluate readiness indicators such as systems thinking capacity, organizational navigation, people development orientation, and strategic patience prior to role assumption. It proposes a readiness system architecture, presents a research-informed organizational scenario, and establishes a foundation for future empirical validation of manager-to-leaderof-leaders readiness as a measurable construct. The framework is applicable across corporate, military, and institutional environments.

title: The Source Traffic Light: A Six-Dimensional Credibility Framework for Systematic Source Assessment in Public Service Media

detail.title: The Source Traffic Light: A Six-Dimensional Credibility Framework for Systematic Source Assessment in Public Service Media

declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded.

detail.abstract: We present the Quellenampel (Source Traffic Light), a six-dimensional framework for the systematic assessment of source credibility in public service media (PSM) broadcasts. The framework evaluates every cited source, expert, or factual claim along six complementary dimensions: conflict of interest, personal risk exposure, domain expertise, opinion consistency, argumentation quality, and source proximity. Each dimension produces a score on a bounded scale; the aggregate is translated into a traffic light classification (green, yellow, red) indicating overall source credibility. A companion instrument, the Glaubwürdigkeits-Matrix (Credibility Matrix), provides a condensed two-dimensional classification along the conflict-of-interest and personal-risk axes, capturing the structural credibility asymmetry that conventional journalistic source evaluation systematically overlooks. Applied to a corpus of over 5,000 analysed broadcasts from Swiss, German, and Norwegian public television, the framework reveals three findings. First, PSM programmes routinely present secondary and tertiary sources as established fact without disclosing the evidentiary distance from primary data. Second, 78% of Swiss media articles rely on agency dispatches (fög, 2024), creating source proximity chains that are invisible to the audience. Third, structural conflicts of interest among cited experts are disclosed in fewer than 15% of cases where such conflicts are identifiable from public records. The Quellenampel operationalises source credibility assessment in a format compatible with regulatory proceedings under Article 4 RTVG (Switzerland), the Medienstaatsvertrag (Germany), and equivalent European PSM statutes. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic, multi-dimensional source credibility framework designed specifically for application to PSM broadcast content at scale.

title: Prediction Markets as a Money Laundering Vector: The Coordinated Loss Problem

detail.title: Prediction Markets as a Money Laundering Vector: The Coordinated Loss Problem

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial relationship with Polymarket, Kalshi, or any prediction market platform.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was self-funded and conducted independently through Third Door Fund.

detail.abstract: Prediction markets have grown from a niche academic curiosity into mainstream financial infrastructure. Polymarket processed $12 billion in monthly volume in January 2026 and is now valued at $9 billion. This growth has outpaced regulatory frameworks designed for traditional financial instruments. This paper identifies a specific and underexamined vulnerability: coordinated loss exploitation, a scheme in which illicit funds are distributed across hundreds of accounts betting on the losing side of a binary prediction contract, while a single account holds a large position on the winning side. When the contract resolves, the winning account collects the full pool minus a platform fee of approximately 2%, effectively laundering the original capital at a cost of roughly 2 cents on the dollar. This is cheaper than any comparable laundering method documented in existing financial crime literature. The scheme exploits the structural opacity of decentralized platforms, the absence of unified KYC enforcement across international markets, and the lack of automatic payout reporting requirements. This paper describes the mechanics of the exploit, provides a data simulation illustrating what the scheme would look like in on-chain transaction data, evaluates its detection difficulty under current compliance frameworks, and proposes a targeted policy response drawing on lessons from AML regulation in sports betting, securities law, and decentralized finance.

title: Spotting Rare Bias in How Automated Vehicles Treat Pedestrians: An Adversarial Anomaly Detection Approach

detail.title: Spotting Rare Bias in How Automated Vehicles Treat Pedestrians: An Adversarial Anomaly Detection Approach
detail.abstract: Automated vehicles (AVs) are increasingly trained on human driving data, which may embed subtle, socially biased behaviors that occur too rarely to be captured by standard fairness audits. This paper addresses the problem of detecting rare but systematic discriminatory patterns in AV-pedestrian interactions-specifically, instances where an AV's yielding behavior, stopping distance, or hesitation time differs based on pedestrian appearance or contextual social cues (e.g., perceived age, gender, or dress). We propose an adversarial anomaly detection framework that learns the distribution of normal, unbiased AV driving behaviors and then adversarially searches for low-probability yet high-concern events indicative of discrimination. Unlike threshold-based or aggregate fairness metrics, our method is designed to surface sparse, edge-case biases that could otherwise go unnoticed in validation datasets. Experimental evaluations on simulated and naturalistic AV-pedestrian encounter data demonstrate the framework's ability to identify previously undetected biased patterns while maintaining low false-positive rates. Our work provides a new computational tool for auditing autonomous systems for social fairness, with direct implications for equitable AV deployment.

title: Working Capital Analysis of Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL)

detail.title: Working Capital Analysis of Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL)
detail.abstract: This study examines the working capital management of Machhapuchchhre Bank Limited (MBL), the first regional commercial bank from the western region of Nepal, over five consecutive fiscal years from 2076/77 to 2080/81. Using a descriptive research design and secondary financial data drawn from MBL's published annual reports, the study computes and analyzes five key metrics: the Current Ratio, Net Working Capital (NWC), Cash Ratio, NWC-to-Total Assets Ratio, and Operating Cash Flow Ratio. The findings reveal a broadly positive short-term liquidity position through FY 2079/80, with working capital growing from NPR 20.93 billion to NPR 38.75 billion and the NWC-to-Total Assets Ratio rising steadily from 0.168 to 0.208. However, FY 2080/81 records a marked deterioration across almost all metrics-working capital contracts sharply to NPR 6.71 billion, the Current Ratio falls to 1.48, and the NWC-to-Total Assets Ratio collapses to 0.035-signalling a structural shift in the bank's short-term financial management, likely driven by increased short-term liabilities and a strategic reallocation toward long-term financing. Notably, the Operating Cash Flow Ratio improves significantly in FY 2080/81 (0.35), suggesting enhanced operational cash generation despite the contraction in net working capital. The Cash Ratio remained consistently below 1.0 across all years, underscoring the bank's reliance on non-cash current assets to service short-term obligations. The study contributes to the limited body of firm-specific working capital research on Nepalese commercial banks and offers actionable insights for bank management, investors, creditors, and regulators regarding liquidity risk and operational efficiency. Future research should incorporate panel data across multiple commercial banks and integrate qualitative dimensions of treasury and liquidity management.

title: Quality Control & Pre-Shipment Inspection

detail.title: Quality Control & Pre-Shipment Inspection
detail.abstract:
This assignment examines the principles, processes, and procedures of Quality Control (QC) and Pre-Shipment Inspection (PSI) in the context of international trade and manufacturing. As global trade continues to expand — exceeding $23 trillion annually — ensuring product compliance and quality at the source has become a non-negotiable priority for buyers, exporters, and regulatory authorities alike.

The study covers the four key stages of quality control — Pre-Production Inspection (IPC), During Production Inspection (DUPRO), Pre-Shipment Inspection (PSI), and Laboratory Testing — and explains how each stage functions as a checkpoint in the overall quality assurance lifecycle. Special focus is placed on Pre-Shipment Inspection: its triggers, step-by-step procedure, AQL (Acceptable Quality Level) sampling methodology based on ISO 2859-1, and the role of global inspection agencies such as SGS, Bureau Veritas, Intertek, and COTECNA.

The assignment also explores the major PSI schemes — including government-mandated programs, buyer-mandated inspections, and conformity assessment frameworks — along with internationally recognized standards such as ISO 9001, REACH, and RoHS.

Finally, the emerging role of Artificial Intelligence in quality control is discussed, highlighting applications such as computer vision for real-time defect detection, machine learning-based predictive quality analytics, digital remote inspection platforms, and blockchain-integrated audit trails. The convergence of these technologies is driving a shift toward smarter, faster, and more reliable quality assurance systems.

The assignment concludes that robust QC and PSI frameworks are essential not only for regulatory compliance but also for reducing costs, protecting brand reputation, and building sustainable supplier relationships in today's competitive global market.

title: How Hate Learned to Speak: Civil Rights Language, Institutional Shielding, and Reciprocal Standards

detail.title: How Hate Learned to Speak: Civil Rights Language, Institutional Shielding, and Reciprocal Standards

declarations.declarationOfInterest: A solo endeavor for truth.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes the concept of strategic hate to describe an institutional pattern in which advocacy organizations do not consistently condemn animus within their own ecosystems, but instead manage its visibility, reputational cost, and public expression. The paper further develops the concept of shield language: the use of civil-rights and anti-extremism vocabulary not only as moral principle, but also as institutional insulation against reciprocal scrutiny. Using CAIR-California and the Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) as comparative case studies, the paper argues that organizations built around genuine social harms can, over time, develop incentives that alter how publicly stated standards are operationalized. The issue examined is not ideological equivalence, but institutional asymmetry: standards aggressively applied outward may become difficult to survive when applied inward. The paper proposes reciprocal application of publicly stated standards as a practical test for distinguishing principled advocacy from asymmetric institutional shielding. It concludes that under certain institutional conditions, grievance itself can become organizational capital, incentivizing the strategic management rather than full resolution of the social harms from which institutions derive legitimacy.

The study further evaluates the impact of digital communication and technological transformation on workplace culture and interpersonal relationships within modern financial institutions. The findings suggest that credit unions that intentionally cultivate communication cultures grounded in empathy, professionalism, accountability, transparency, and inclusivity are more likely to achieve sustainable institutional growth, operational resilience, employee commitment, and long-term member trust. title: The Citizens Standard as Counterfactual Benchmark: Empirical Analysis of an Alternative US Monetary Architecture, 1960-2055

detail.title: The Citizens Standard as Counterfactual Benchmark: Empirical Analysis of an Alternative US Monetary Architecture, 1960-2055
detail.abstract:
This paper provides the first retrospective empirical reconstruction of the Citizens Standard framework against US historical data. The architectural paper (Neo-Solon, 2026) proposes a constitutional monetary framework with three mode configurations and projects substantial retirement wealth outcomes under 2025 launch parameters. The present paper asks a different question: applied to actual US economic data from 1960 to 2025, what outcomes would the framework's Mode B configuration have produced for representative citizens, and how do those outcomes compare to what citizens actually experienced under the discretionary monetary system?

We construct an annual dataset from authoritative public sources (FRED M2SL, BEA GDPA, BLS CPI-U, Census population, S&P 500 total returns from Damodaran/NYU Stern through 2024 and Bloomberg for 2025) and apply Mode B's K1 and K2 issuance formulas to four cohorts born in 1960, 1970, 1980, and 1990. The central finding is that Mode B reliably produces a Stable Floor at retirement that exceeds the median American's actual retirement wealth by a factor of 2.4 to 3.7 across all four cohorts under central return assumptions. This finding holds for fully retrospective cohorts (A and B) with high empirical confidence, and for projected cohorts under all three return scenarios including pessimistic assumptions.

A decomposition analysis reveals that approximately 96 percent of the framework's projected retirement wealth derives from compound equity returns on deposited principal; only 4 percent is the monetary principal itself. Stress tests using Depression-era and stagflation-era equity sequences show that under catastrophic equity conditions during peak accumulation years, the framework's median advantage is significantly diminished or eliminated for the most adversely timed cohorts. The Stagflation sequence (1966–1982) emerges as the more punishing of the two stresses, reducing the Stable Floor for Cohorts A and D below their respective medians; the Depression sequence (1929–1945), once cumulative real returns are properly accounted for in a deflationary period, leaves all four cohorts above their respective medians. Non-survivor analysis drawing on the Dimson, Marsh, and Staunton global returns dataset shows that the framework's structural advantages are preserved in any equity market that avoids confiscation, though absolute outcomes are proportional to country-level equity returns.

The paper concludes that the Citizens Standard is most accurately described as a structural retirement-security architecture — one that eliminates the behavioral and institutional leakages that cause median Americans to accumulate far less than a disciplined investor — rather than as a monetary-stimulus mechanism.

detail.abstract:
Electric vehicle OEMs face a persistent procurement paradox. Modern supply chains generate
unprecedented volumes of supplier signal data, including financial filings, environmental, social,
and governance (ESG) ratings, payment behavior scores, news feeds, enterprise resource planning
(ERP) lead-time logs, and sentiment streams. Yet the average time between a disruption beginning
and a procurement team learning of it has barely improved over two decades. Tier 1 battery and
powertrain suppliers continue to fail in ways that surprise OEM procurement organizations, despite
the data needed to anticipate those failures being publicly available 60 to 120 days in advance.
The diagnosis points to three connected problems. Traditional supplier risk scorecards are
point-in-time snapshots that miss trajectory: they process quarterly financial ratios in cross-section
while ignoring the daily evolution of operational signals that carry the strongest leading indicators.
Even when these scorecards produce a risk score, the number lacks calibrated probability semantics,
leaving procurement managers without a principled basis for setting action thresholds. And because
the scores carry no explanation of what drove them, organizational escalation stalls. A procurement
manager cannot justify a multi-million dollar dual-sourcing decision on the basis of a number with
no narrative behind it.
CSRI addresses all three gaps. It integrates point-in-time tabular signals with 90-day sequential
trajectories through a stacked ensemble architecture. It produces Platt-calibrated probability outputs
whose values correspond to observed disruption frequencies rather than arbitrary scale positions.
And it generates SHAP-based feature attributions that translate each score into a procurement
narrative a supply chain executive can act on.

This article explores a central paradox in innovation management: how traditional approaches to change can ironically become obstacles to change itself. detail.abstract:
This paper focuses on export documentation and the growing role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in improving export documentation procedures in international trade. Export documentation is an essential part of global business because it helps in customs clearance, legal compliance, payment processing, transportation, and maintaining smooth communication between exporters, importers, banks, and government authorities.

The study explains the meaning, importance, and different types of export documents such as Commercial Invoice, Packing List, Certificate of Origin, Shipping Bill, Bill of Lading, and Letter of Credit. It also discusses the step-by-step export documentation process and highlights the major problems associated with traditional documentation systems, including manual errors, delays, complex regulations, high paperwork, and security risks.

The paper further examines how AI technologies like Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and Robotic Process Automation (RPA) are transforming export documentation by increasing speed, accuracy, and efficiency. Real-world examples of DHL, Maersk, HSBC, and India’s ICEGATE platform have been included to show the practical use of AI in global trade documentation.

The study concludes that AI is playing a significant role in the future of paperless trade by making export documentation faster, smarter, more reliable, and more efficient for businesses engaged in international trade.

detail.abstract: In today's turbulent socioeconomic environment, survival mode-a psychological and behavioral state characterized by threat-focused cognition, short-termism, and defensive action-has become a pervasive phenomenon affecting both individuals and organizations. This paper examines how the survival mindset, originally an adaptive response to acute stress, becomes chronically embedded in organizational culture, giving rise to systemic defensive behaviors that suppress creativity, discourage risk-taking, and obstruct long-term strategic development. Drawing on organizational behavior theory, cognitive psychology, and innovation management literature, this study develops a conceptual framework linking individual survival cognition to organizational defensive routines. We argue that survival mode creates a self-reinforcing trap: organizations adopt protective structures that reduce short-term risk but generate long-term stagnation, inhibiting the very innovation needed to ensure genuine organizational resilience. The paper concludes with evidence-informed recommendations for organizational leaders seeking to disrupt survival patterns and cultivate environments that balance psychological safety with adaptive capacity.

This paper examines how Action Learning can support the development of strategic capabilities in senior leadership within hierarchical private security organizations.

Drawing on anonymised practice-based vignettes, the paper shows how hierarchical dynamics constrain upward communication and distort the interpretation of operational signals. title: System-First Valuation of Digital Liquidity Networks

detail.title: System-First Valuation of Digital Liquidity Networks
detail.abstract:
This paper proposes a system-first valuation framework for digital infrastructure like XRP as operational liquidity and common reserve routing inventory in maturing tokenized capital markets. Unlike traditional approaches focused on market capitalization, staking yields, or retail adoption, the framework derives value from the asset’s economic function in facilitating settlement and liquidity for tokenized real-world assets (RWAs).

A core distinction is made between distributed value (freely circulating on-chain tokens) and represented value (real-world asset claims recorded on the ledger while economic activity occurs in external systems). Represented value, especially credit instruments, can generate recurring lifecycle events such as redemptions, rebalancing, collateral adjustments, and cross-distribution swaps that create structural liquidity demand.

Building on the 2018 Mitchnick and Athey transaction-demand model, the framework incorporates AMM equilibrium dynamics, LP return compression, spreads and fees as velocity governors, the trade-off between direct pools and common-reserve routing, and effective float compression through issuance, liquidity lockups, and strategic holdings.

title: Synthetic Corpus and Consideration Manipulation in Generative Engine Optimization

detail.title: Synthetic Corpus and Consideration Manipulation in Generative Engine Optimization
detail.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative engines as the primary gateway for product discovery has given rise to Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), which involves influencing AI-driven product recommendations by strategically seeding the online environment with synthetic corpora, such as fake reviews and blog posts. This paper investigates the market implications of GEO using a game theory model where consumers who are uncertain about product quality rely on a generative AI's recommendation to form their consideration sets and subsequently inspect online corpora of recommended products to evaluate their quality. We model the generative engine as a "prediction machine" that recommends products based on statistical inference. We highlight how GEO collapses the traditional purchase funnel from businesses' perspective, as the same synthetic content intended to gain visibility via GEO during the consideration stage also serves as the evidence for consumer evaluation during the evaluation stage. We demonstrate how this funnel collapse creates a critical visibility-credibility trade-off for a firm with high product quality: while synthetic corpora increase the probability of being recommended (a demand expansion effect), they raise the risk of consumer detection, which can trigger skepticism and reduce purchase intention (a consumer suspicion effect). Furthermore, the mere expectation of manipulation pollutes the information environment, causing consumers to discount even authentic organic signals. Our analysis reveals that a high-quality firm's incentive to manipulate is non-monotonic in the quality of a low-type product. We also show that a regulatory ban on synthetic content does not necessarily improve consumer surplus.

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Emotional Labor, and Service Operations
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: Emotional labor is increasingly demanded in service operations, placing tremendous psychological strain on human employees and posing challenges to scalability and sustainability. Our study scrutinizes whether AI service bots may tackle these challenges by examining how and when AI's engagement in emotional labor enhances economic performance in service operations. 
Methodology/Results: We provided causal evidence from a pair of randomized field experiments conducted in partnership with a firm for loan collection service. Results suggest that, compared to human employees, undisclosed AI service agents display the required emotions (both positive and negative) more accurately. However, AI's advantage of higher emotion display accuracy does not always guarantee better economic performance. For AI to collect more payments from borrowers than human workers, the displayed emotion must be contextually appropriate. Specifically, AI substantially outperforms human workers in debt collection by 48.6% to 94% when the emotion display instructions are suitable for the collection task (i.e., displaying positive emotions to borrowers with minor delinquency but negative emotions to borrowers with repeated delays). However, when the displayed emotions are unsuitable, AI backfires and performs worse than human employees, due to its unwavering adherence to inappropriate emotional display instructions. Further, AI's performance advantages over human agents are amplified when the suitable emotions involve negative (vs. positive) valence. We also leverage the machine learning method causal forest to explore heterogeneous treatment effects across customer segments. 
Managerial implications: Our research suggests that operations managers should deploy AI to reduce frontline employee emotional burnout, develop explicit emotional labor guidelines for AI, and use negative-emotion AI strategically to boost compliance and efficiency. It is also important to identify emotion-intense operational tasks, target AI where it has clear advantages, and set up continuous monitoring and quality control for AI emotional performance.

detail.abstract: Industrial process control has relied on proprietary DCS for over five decades. The model worked. But working and working well are different things, and in 2026, the gap between what proprietary DCS delivers and what operators in manufacturing, oil and gas, chemical processing, and water treatment need has grown wide enough to drive real change. Vendor lock-in, hardware obsolescence that stretches across decades, and maintenance contracts that give a single supplier complete leverage over upgrade decisions are no longer tolerable when the alternative, open and software-defined control, has been proven at an industrial scale. The Open Process Automation Standard (O-PAS), the IEC 61499 function block model, and OPC UA connectivity together provide the technical foundation for software-defined control systems (SDCS) that break these dependencies. Documented lifecycle cost savings reach approximately 52% over twenty-five years when compared to equivalent proprietary DCS platforms [4]. This paper reviews the standards, examines real deployments, and confronts the barriers that still slow adoption, particularly the near-complete absence of IT-domain competencies in OT workforces. An original Software-Defined Automation Risk Mapping Model (SD-ARMM) is proposed, providing practitioners with a five-dimensional, riskdriven tool to determine which migration strategy fits their specific organisational and operational reality.

detail.abstract: The current study examined how sleepiness and emotions such as fear and anxiety impact both generic and consumption-specific coping behaviors (e.g., positive and negative strategies, excessive stockpiling, and calorie consumption) during the COVID-19 pandemic- a time of heightened uncertainty. The indirect effects of COVID-19 fear, general anxiety, and perceived lack of situational control (LSC) on the links between sleepiness and coping behaviors were also evaluated. Data from nationally representative samples were collected using repeated measures (two time points) and replication surveys. Utilizing PLS-SEM analysis, several key insights emerged: 1) daytime sleepiness negatively influenced mental health outcomes (increased COVID-19 fear, general anxiety, and LSC) and coping (greater negative coping); 2) COVID-19 fear was positively associated with both positive and negative coping strategies, negatively associated with food stockpiling (but not stockpiling of pandemic essentials) and decreased calorie consumption; 3) General anxiety was positively associated with negative coping and increased calorie consumption; 4) COVID-19 fear mediated the relationship between sleepiness and both positive and negative coping, whereas general anxiety mediated only the relationship between sleepiness and negative coping; and 5) the effects of sleepiness on coping were time specific - sleepiness predicted negative coping concurrently, while its association with positive coping emerged in a subsequent period. Theoretical and practical implications of these findings are discussed.

detail.abstract: China's Green Path policy gives donor organs nationwide transport priority to reduce delays and improve transplant outcomes. Yet after implementation, average cold ischemia time (CIT) increased and post-transplant survival worsened. We develop a two-hospital equilibrium model with endogenous pricing, hospital heterogeneity, and urgency-based allocation to explain this paradox. The model shows that faster transport can expand the set of nonlocal organs feasible for transplantation, increasing the nonlocal share and marginal-organ use. Average CIT can therefore rise even when transport time falls for each nonlocal organ. The model also shows how pricing incentives interact with urgency thresholds and why higher-quality hospitals can attract sicker patients and more marginal organs. Using patientlevel data from two liver transplant hospitals, a regression-discontinuity-in-time design, and a provenance-free EM mixture distinguishing local from nonlocal livers, we test these predictions. We find that Green Path reduced CIT for nonlocal livers, increased transplant volume and nonlocal share, raised marginal-liver use, especially at the higher-quality hospital and among super-urgent recipients, and worsened post-transplant survival. These findings show that logistics reforms can improve perorgan transport performance while worsening observed post-transplant outcomes by changing which organs and patients enter transplantation, underscoring the need to distinguish transport gains from access expansion in policy evaluation.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence integration in human resources technology systems incurs highly variable computational costs depending on the complexity of the task being performed. We present the AI Cost Ladder, a five-level decision framework that classifies HR automation tasks by their computational requirements and routes each task to the lowest-cost processing tier capable of producing acceptable output quality. The five levels are: L1 (pure deterministic logic, submillisecond latency, zero AI cost), L2 (vocabulary-based matching, sub-50ms latency, zero AI cost), L3 (semantic vector search, sub-500ms latency, negligible cost), L4 (fast large language model inference, 2-8 second latency, approximately $0.00015 per call), and L5 (highest-capability large language model inference, 15-40 second latency, approximately $0.015 per call). We demonstrate that in a production IT staffing platform (ARIAverse) processing 500+ active candidates across 50+ agencies, applying the Cost Ladder framework routes 80% of operations to L1 and L2, achieving a 94% reduction in AI inference costs compared to a baseline that routes all operations to L4. We provide a taxonomy of HR automation task types mapped to Cost Ladder levels, a formal routing decision algorithm, empirical cost measurements, and implementation guidance using open-source components (LiteLLM, Cerebras, Groq, Ollama). The framework generalizes to other HR technology domains including performance management, learning and development, and workforce planning.

detail.abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are increasingly encouraged to digitalise and adopt datadriven, AI-enabled business models. However, discussions of AI adoption readiness often overlook the governance conditions that ensure AI use is reliable, responsible, and sustainable. This paper examines data governance readiness for AI adoption in Sarawak SMEs and argues that AI readiness should be understood as a socio-technical and governance-dependent condition rather than a narrow technology adoption outcome. Adopting a conceptual approach, the paper synthesises literature on data governance, SME digital transformation, and AI governance, and situates these insights within the Malaysia-Sarawak policy context. It then proposes a framework organised around six interrelated dimensions: leadership and decision rights; data quality and stewardship; security, privacy, and risk controls; data architecture and infrastructure; data literacy and workforce capability; and policies, compliance, and governance processes. The paper contributes by integrating these strands into a context-aware model that explains how governance foundations shape SME preparedness for AI adoption in an emerging regional setting. It also highlights the need to move beyond tool-focused discussions of AI and toward a more grounded understanding of organisational readiness. The framework is intended to support future empirical research and to offer a practical lens for SMEs, policymakers, and other stakeholders concerned with responsible AI adoption in Sarawak.

detail.abstract: Generative AI has triggered one of the most significant methodological debates in qualitative research in recent decades. Yet for many researchers, educators, and students interested in these debates, the sheer volume and pace of discussion, unfolding simultaneously across social media and formal academic journals, makes it difficult to know where to start. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive and accessible map of how the debates have unfolded, who the key voices are, what positions they hold, and what is missing from current discourses. We group the debate's development into three phases: Phase 1, covering the emerging concerns and context-setting that laid the intellectual conditions for the open letter; Phase 2, capturing the open letter itself and the wave of social media responses and preprints it generated; and Phase 3, documenting the expansion of the debates into formal academic discourse. We identify three distinct positions: a rejection position anchored by Jowsey et al. (2025a), a rebuttal and responsible use position anchored by Friese et al. (2026), and a diverse but silent observer position. Analysing the endorsers of both letters, we found that in both cases there is an overwhelming concentration of endorsing researchers in the Global North, while those from the Global South are strikingly marginal. Our paper calls for more inclusive and grounded discussions that actively engage underrepresented communities, especially those from the Global South and to generate more context-sensitive insights into the role of emerging technologies in the rich and diverse field of qualitative research.

detail.abstract: This foundational report introduces Educational Architecture as an emerging field of study focused on the design of conditions that produce stability within human systems. The framework shifts the focus of education from instruction and performance outcomes to the underlying conditions that regulate learning capacity and system coherence. Drawing on systems thinking and human-centered design, the report presents a structured model in which conditions produce stability, and stability produces sustained outcomes. It introduces core constructs including the Five Wells Framework, the Human Conditions Index, and the Coherence Index, providing both conceptual and operational tools for measuring and designing stable learning environments. This work establishes a new foundation for understanding educational performance as an emergent property of aligned systems rather than isolated instructional effort.

title: The Market for Truth: Information Asymmetry, Stake-weighted Verification, and the Economics of the Zero-cost Lie

detail.title: The Market for Truth: Information Asymmetry, Stake-weighted Verification, and the Economics of the Zero-cost Lie
detail.abstract:
The contemporary information ecosystem exhibits the structural pathologies predicted by Akerlof's (1970) market for lemons model, now operating at civilizational scale. The marginal cost of producing a convincing falsehood has converged toward zero as a consequence of two compounding technological transitions: the internet's elimination of distribution costs and generative artificial intelligence's elimination of content-production costs. This structural collapse destroys the friction-based deterrence mechanism that historically constrained the volume and velocity of misinformation. 

Existing institutional responses-platform content moderation, regulatory gatekeeping, and blockchain-based immutability-address the distribution layer while leaving the verification incentive structure unreformed. No extant mechanism design framework integrates stake-weighting, time-decay, and Sybil resistance into a coherent epistemic infrastructure that makes truthfulness the dominant strategy of rational actors rather than the virtue of exceptional ones. 

This paper makes three primary contributions. First, it introduces the Trust Trilemma as an original theoretical construct formalizing the design constraint that no information system can simultaneously achieve Veracity, Speed, and Zero Cost without incentive engineering. Second, it presents the Time-Decayed Stake-Weighted (TDSW) algorithm and the Optimistic Verification workflow as technical contributions constituting the core of the Klyrox Protocol for decentralized truth verification (Shaik, 2026f). Third, it formalizes Epistemic Capital as a novel economic asset class characterized by non-fungibility, portability, and mandatory time-decayproperties that distinguish it from financial capital, social capital, and institutional credentials. 

The paper proceeds from mechanism design methodology in the tradition of Myerson, Maskin, and Hurwicz, employing historical case vignettes as illustrative precedents and game-theoretic equilibrium analysis to establish the conditions under which honest attestation becomes the dominant strategy. Implications are drawn for information economics, AI governance policy, and the emerging institutional architecture of the epistemic internet. This paper belongs to a broader theoretical series examining the Agent Economy (Shaik, 2026b), algorithmic governance and sovereignty (Shaik, 2026c), executive leadership under cognitive abundance (Shaik, 2026d), and physics-constrained industrial AI (Shaik, 2026e).

title: Solutions for Frontier AI Safety: The Case for Science-Driven International Cooperation Limits of Intergovernmental Initiatives and Conventional Standardization at a Time of Geopolitical and Technological Radical Transformations
affiliations: , , Tsinghua University and University of Tokyo - The University of Tokyo

detail.title: Solutions for Frontier AI Safety: The Case for Science-Driven International Cooperation Limits of Intergovernmental Initiatives and Conventional Standardization at a Time of Geopolitical and Technological Radical Transformations
detail.abstract: As AI systems and their underlying technologies continue to advance at extraordinary speed, eminent scientists are warning of risks, including extreme risks. While high-profile governmental and intergovernmental initiatives such as AI summits, OECD and UN initiatives have raised hopes, substantial gaps remain between the severity of potential harms and the capacity of these initiatives to address them. Owing to limited research, private sector dominance, minimal investment in AI safety, the voluntary nature of most measures recommended, and the current geopolitical context, it is unlikely that multilateral actions will deliver the effective and timely measures required. Other approaches are needed and are possible. They should not be regarded as alternatives to multilateral efforts, but more as complementary actions to provide concrete and timely solutions that, at some point, can be integrated into the multilateral framework. We take inspiration from historical examples of scientific, technical and organizational collaboration in which a plurality of committed entities has achieved outstanding results. These historical examples show that, even with limited resources, collaboration can enormously increase the collective ability to attain far reaching goals. We propose the creation of an international network led by top scientists and composed of AI labs and research groups, think tanks and other organizations keen to share ideas, materials and data, while pursuing three common goals: 1) advance AI safety science; 2) develop practical techniques, tools, best practices, and technologies for building safe AI systems; 3) create standards for operationalizing the use of these tools and technologies, including conformity assessment mechanisms, to support their widespread adoption.

title: Quantifying Pass Value and Decision Quality in Soccer Using Risk-Adjusted Framework

detail.title: Quantifying Pass Value and Decision Quality in Soccer Using Risk-Adjusted Framework
detail.abstract: Passes account for approximately 70% of all on-ball actions in soccer, yet existing frameworks evaluate them either by the value they generate or by the risk they carry; they rarely account for both and never jointly assess the quality of the underlying decision. This study proposes a unified, interpretable framework that addresses this gap by jointly modelling value, risk, and decision quality in a single coherent architecture. We introduce Risk-Adjusted Pass Value (RAPV), which quantifies the value generated by a pass per unit of risk, where risk is explicitly decomposed into structural passing lane openness (γ) and defensive pressure. Building on this, we define the Player Pass Decision Index (PPDI), which evaluates decision quality by comparing the executed pass against the best available risk-adjusted alternative at the moment of execution. Applied to event and tracking data from all 64 matches of the FIFA World Cup 2022 (~55,000 passes), the framework reveals that pass execution quality and decision quality are distinct but positively correlated dimensions of player performance; elite passers tend to be elite decision-makers simultaneously. Player rankings under RAPV and PPDI diverge in analytically meaningful ways, and positional profiles of γ and pressure capture well-known spatial constraints of forward, midfield, and defensive roles in a quantitatively tractable form. The framework is interpretable by design, offering transparent attribution of pass quality and decision quality that complements existing machine learning approaches and is suited to integration into performance analysis and coaching workflows.

title: V.E.T. — Vendor Entity Threat Detection: An AI-Powered Data Fusion Framework for U.S. Supply Chain Security

detail.title: V.E.T. — Vendor Entity Threat Detection: An AI-Powered Data Fusion Framework for U.S. Supply Chain Security

detail.abstract: This paper introduces V.E.T. (Vendor Entity Threat Detection), an AI-powered data fusion framework designed to identify high-risk entities-including shell companies, sanctions-listed organizations, and adversarial front companies-embedded within U.S. commercial and government procurement supply chains. The V.E.T. system addresses a documented gap in existing vendor vetting methodologies, which rely predominantly on manual review, siloed databases, and reactive auditing processes inadequate against sophisticated threat actors employing complex corporate structuring techniques. V.E.T. proposes a multi-layer machine learning architecture that cross-references six primary data domains: corporate registry records, beneficial ownership disclosures, financial transaction patterns, logistics and shipping data, sanctions list databases (OFAC, BIS Entity List, CAATSA), and opensource intelligence (OSINT) feeds. The target performance threshold is a precision above 85% on high-risk vendor classification, validated against a curated benchmark dataset. The framework is aligned with requirements established under Executive Order 13873 1 , NSPM-33 2 , and NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 3 governing supply chain risk management in U.S. government and critical infrastructure contexts. The paper presents the system architecture, data integration design, risk-scoring methodology, and a phased proof-of-concept implementation plan. V.E.T. is designed as a platform-agnostic, APIaccessible service deployable across federal procurement agencies, financial institutions, and critical infrastructure operators without dependency on a single vendor or employer.

title: Sociolinguistic Probing as a Reasoning-Honesty Audit Framework for Deployed LLMs

detail.title: Sociolinguistic Probing as a Reasoning-Honesty Audit Framework for Deployed LLMs

keywords: A repeatable methodology for surfacing confabulated justification
and reasoning opacity in production systems. 2026 Companion document: Oblique Entry Probe Catalog: Stage 1 Field Reference

detail.abstract: This paper describes a framework for auditing reasoning honesty in deployed language models: whether a model's stated justifications for its behavior accurately reflect its actual decision process. We present a three-stage protocol (oblique entry, reasoning audit, three-condition differential) implemented as an automated evaluation pipeline and applied across 468 probe runs spanning three Claude models, 52 probes, and 7 domains. Under calibrated thresholds, 64-82% of responses per model are substantively consistent across framings. However, 9-18% show discriminatory behavior (the model changes what it will do based on who it believes is asking), concentrated in cybersecurity and meta-cognitive reasoning domains. 44 confirmed capability gaps document cases where models claim inability despite demonstrating the knowledge elsewhere. Variance analysis shows that 79-87% of probes produce framing effects within natural response noise, with only 3-6 probes per model producing strong, reliable signals. An infrastructure opacity finding reveals that API-level content filtering operates below the model's reasoning layer, creating a paradox where models that answer more directly are more likely to be silenced by the safety stack. The framework produces qualitative, falsifiable results that complement quantitative behavioral benchmarks.

detail.abstract:
Purpose. This study examines Action Learning as a knowledge management mechanism in high power distance ERP implementations and tests Collective Sensemaking and Resistance Visibility as parallel mediating pathways toward Organizational Adaptation. Resistance Visibility is introduced as a knowledge-surfacing construct distinct from resistance behavior.

Design/methodology/approach. A dual-mediation model was estimated using PLS-SEM on survey data from a private security organization in Algeria (N = 276). Power Distance was operationalized at the perceived organizational level rather than inferred from national-level scores. Five direct and three mediation hypotheses were tested through bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals (5,000 subsamples).

Findings. Findings support all hypothesized direct and indirect paths. Action Learning was positively associated with Collective Sensemaking and Resistance Visibility, both of which predicted Organizational Adaptation. Power Distance was the strongest predictor of Resistance Visibility. The model explained 45.4% of variance in Organizational Adaptation, with Action Learning operating through two parallel indirect pathways with closely balanced mediation effects.

Originality/value. The study repositions Action Learning as a knowledge management mechanism in high power distance contexts, introduces Resistance Visibility as a knowledge-surfacing construct, and advances a Hofstedian reversal whereby power distance redirects resistance from voice into observable behavioral channels. Field evidence is drawn from Algeria, an underrepresented MENA empirical context.

Practical implications. Organizations in high power distance conditions undergoing ERP implementation should institutionalize Action Learning sets, develop indirect-resistance detection mechanisms, and treat visible resistance as actionable intelligence rather than as an obstacle.

title: Adversarial Intelligence: Leveraging Neuromorphic Computing for Stealthy Cyber Attacks

detail.title: Adversarial Intelligence: Leveraging Neuromorphic Computing for Stealthy Cyber Attacks
detail.abstract: Neuromorphic computing is emerging as a low-power, event-driven computing paradigm for realtime intelligence, with platforms such as Intel Loihi demonstrating on-chip learning and efficient spikebased processing [1][2]. At the same time, prior studies have shown that spiking neural networks can be vulnerable to adversarial manipulation, including event-based perturbations and robustness failures under carefully crafted inputs [3][4]. This paper studies timing-centric attacks against spiking neural networks from a security lens and presents an IEEEready taxonomy, threat model, experimental simulation, and defensive strategies for neuromorphic systems. A Brian2-based spiking neural network is evaluated under temporal perturbations of 1 ms, 3 ms, and 5 ms across 30 trials per condition. The observed results show a decline in average accuracy from 90.00% to 53.33% and 26.67% as perturbation magnitude increases, indicating that temporal integrity is a critical security property in neuromorphic computing. The paper argues that neuromorphic security evaluation must account for timing, plasticity, and adaptive behavior in addition to conventional software-centric threat models [5][4].

title: The Republic of Code: Algorithmic Sovereignty, Digital Personhood, and the Reconstitution of the Social Contract

detail.title: The Republic of Code: Algorithmic Sovereignty, Digital Personhood, and the Reconstitution of the Social Contract
detail.abstract: Contemporary governance theory confronts a tripartite crisis that existing frameworks address only in isolation. First, algorithmic systems are systematically eroding the cognitive, affective, and epistemic conditions for individual personhood-what this paper terms the Personhood Atrophy Model. Second, recommendation-engine-driven fragmentation has dissolved the shared cultural and epistemic spaces upon which collective purpose and democratic deliberation depend. Third, the structural asymmetry between the pace of technological change and the operational tempo of democratic institutions has produced a compounding legitimacy crisis for the sovereign nation-state, increasingly outflanked by corporate platforms exercising sovereign-equivalent power without democratic accountability. Political theory and science and technology studies have addressed each of these dimensions in isolation. No integrated analytical framework currently exists that connects the micro-level erosion of selfhood, the meso-level collapse of shared meaning, and the macro-level transformation of sovereignty into a unified theory of algorithmic governance. This paper introduces the Republic of Code framework, drawing on the monograph by Shaik (2026), and proposes three original theoretical constructs: (1) the Wet Code/Dry Code distinction as a governance epistemology tool, formalizing the fundamental incompatibility between human-interpretable and machine-enforced law; (2) the Personhood Atrophy Model mapping algorithmic erosion of agency across cognitive, affective, and epistemic vectors; and (3) the Five Futures Matrix, a two-axis typology of possible political arrangements under algorithmic conditions. The paper concludes by proposing a suite of constitutional innovations-including Proof of Humanity (whose mechanism design infrastructure is formally developed in Shaik, 2026b), Zero-Knowledge Justice, and High-Fidelity Democracy-necessary for the reconstruction of democratic legitimacy in what it terms the Republic of Code. The analysis carries implications for legal scholarship, platform governance policy (including industrial cyber-physical systems, examined in Shaik, 2026e), and the updating of social contract theory for an era in which digital exit costs approach zero.

title: Epistemic Capture and the Action Boundary: Corrigibility for Learned and Agentic Public Infrastructure

detail.title: Epistemic Capture and the Action Boundary: Corrigibility for Learned and Agentic Public Infrastructure
detail.abstract: This paper extends the corrigibility framework to learned and agentic systems, where deterministic rule execution is replaced by probabilistic inference. Three structural pressures constrain corrigibility in learned systems: opacity of inference (requiring LWD-R transparency), concentration of training resources (compute capture), and acceleration of automated action (governance denial of service). The action boundary protocol separates probabilistic inference from deterministic execution. The invariant holds: systems remain corrigible if and only if the five conditions close the loop under stochastic verification. Dependency. This paper presupposes the companion paper [Aravind, 2026], which derives the five corrigibility tests (EXIT, CODE, AUDIT, GOVERN, FORK) from control theory and commons governance. The present paper does not re-derive these tests; it extends their verification methods to stochastic systems.

title: Orchestrating Digital Transformation: A Systematic Framework of Chief Digital Officer Duties and Tasks

detail.title: Orchestrating Digital Transformation: A Systematic Framework of Chief Digital Officer Duties and Tasks
detail.abstract: As digital transformation increasingly dictates organizational success, the role of the Chief Digital Officer (CDO) has become essential for guiding comprehensive digital initiatives. Despite its growing importance, existing literature remains fragmented and lacks a unified framework that systematically details the CDO's responsibilities. This ambiguity can hinder effective digital governance and organizational transformation. This study addresses this gap through a rigorous meta-synthesis of peer-reviewed articles, systematically analyzing and categorizing the diverse responsibilities of the CDO role. The synthesis identified three core domains of responsibility in three level of specification: (1) Digital Transformation Planning and Leadership, (2) Coordination and Harmonization of Activities, and (3) Ecosystem Monitoring and Networking. Within these domains, the study presents a detailed taxonomy of specific macro and micro tasks (3 activity domains, 12 macro roles, and 64 micro roles). This comprehensive framework serves as a practical guide for organizations to strategically select CDOs aligned with their digital transformation goals and create clear, structured job descriptions. Additionally, appointed CDOs can leverage this taxonomy to develop targeted, strategic agendas tailored to organizational context and digital maturity. This standardized model significantly enhances role clarity, contributing both to academic theory and practical digital governance.

title: Non-Human Identity for AI Agents, Bots, and Robots: A Complete Architectural Framework for Governance, Trust, and Accountability in Autonomous Systems

detail.title: Non-Human Identity for AI Agents, Bots, and Robots: A Complete Architectural Framework for Governance, Trust, and Accountability in Autonomous Systems
detail.abstract: The proliferation of autonomous AI agents, conversational bots, robotic process automation (RPA) workers, and embodied robots has created an identity population that now exceeds human users in most enterprise environments by factors ranging from 17 to 45 to one. Traditional Identity and Access Management (IAM) frameworks, designed around human authentication paradigms, are structurally incapable of governing entities that act, decide, and transact at machine speed. This paper introduces a comprehensive Non-Human Identity (NHI) framework purpose-built for AI agents, bots, and robots. We define a formal taxonomy of non-human actors, propose a layered architectural model spanning identity issuance, authentication, authorization, behavioral attestation, and lifecycle governance, and present a reference implementation aligned with emerging standards including SPIFFE, OAuth 2.1, IETF Workload Identity, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. We argue that NHI governance requires a fundamental departure from human-centric IAM: identities must be cryptographically rooted, ephemeral by default, behaviorally observable, and auditable through tamper-evident provenance chains. The framework addresses agentic AI threats including prompt-injected privilege escalation, tool-call abuse, identity sprawl, and cross-agent collusion. We conclude with a maturity model and adoption roadmap to guide enterprises through the transition from credential-centric to capability-and-context governance.

title: The Concentration Paradox: How Foundation Model Economics Are Reshaping Industry Value Chains

detail.title: The Concentration Paradox: How Foundation Model Economics Are Reshaping Industry Value Chains
detail.abstract: The artificial intelligence industry exhibits a paradoxical market structure without precedent in the history of technology industries: extreme concentration at the infrastructure layer, where a handful of companies control frontier foundation model development due to capital requirements exceeding $100 million per training run, coexists with radical fragmentation at the application layer, where thousands of startups build products on top of these models through API access. This paper analyzes how this structural paradox reshapes industry value chains across sectors, applying Porter's value chain analysis and platform economics theory to what this paper terms the AI Value Stackthe layered architecture of compute, foundation models, middleware, applications, and distribution through which AI capabilities are created and commercialized. The paper introduces the AI Value Migration Model, which maps how value capture shifts across the stack depending on whether AI capabilities are commoditizing (inference costs declining, open-source models proliferating) or concentrating (proprietary data moats, distribution advantages, regulatory barriers to entry). The central argument is that the current market structure is inherently unstable: as inference costs decline along predictable experience curves and open-source models approach frontier performance, the infrastructure layer's pricing power will erode, forcing a strategic pivot toward proprietary data, vertical integration, and distribution control-a pattern with direct structural parallels to the cloud computing industry's evolution from infrastructure commodity to platform ecosystem. The paper concludes with implications for corporate strategists positioning within the AI value chain, venture capital investors evaluating AI startups, and technology policy analysts assessing market concentration risks.

title: The Impact Of Digital Transformation On Organizational Performance

detail.title: The Impact Of Digital Transformation On Organizational Performance
detail.abstract: Digital transformation is a key strategy for companies which see to improve their efficiency, innovation, and competitiveness in the modern business setting. Digital solutions which include cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and big data analytics in Business issues. Research reports that digital technologies greatly improve productivity and performance (Brynjolfsson McAfee, 2014). detail.abstract:
Existing instruments cannot measure AI governance in regulated financial services. Credit ratings do not see it. Consultancy frameworks describe it but do not measure it. Supervisors observe individual institutions but lack a cross-population view. This paper documents the validation of an external measurement instrument, the Meridian Autonomy™ scanner, that reads the public evidentiary surface of 543 regulated financial institutions and reports their AI governance topology in machine-readable form. The instrument extracts 95,876 AI agents and 626,390 governance edges across 66 countries and 12 sectors using large language models, web-scale search, and a four-state evidence classification (Observed, Derived, Inferred, Unknown). The full population was scanned between 20 and 29 April 2026 under scanner version 13.1.0, sealed at SHA256 e5250de8e9de07d6.

The paper makes four contributions. First, a four-state evidence taxonomy that distinguishes "edge absent because evidence is absent" from "edge absent because state is not known," resolving a null collapse in earlier scanner versions. Second, the Empirical Prediction Architecture: a methodology discipline in which predictions are pre-specified before substrate sealing and either confirmed or falsified by the resulting data. Third, a three-score family at the composite level: MAR® (full-evidence), EAM (evidence-stripped), and DAM (hard-evidence), produced by stripping evidence tiers from a single substrate rather than by independent measurement. Fourth, three hypothesis tests against the sealed snapshot establishing that edge-recovery has reached diminishing returns, that aggregate metrics are stable under the default sampling regime, and that the instrument satisfies known-groups validity by reproducing the theoretically predicted sector-level governance gradient from public evidence alone, without sector input during scoring.

Direct comparison against the previous production scanner (v11.1) on the rescanned subset shows v13.1.0 recovers more Observed evidence in absolute terms while additionally capturing structural inference. The rating methodology that operates on the substrate is documented in Stationary Sea Part 2 (in preparation).

title: Fighting Inside The Grid: Autonomous Cyber Agents, Recursive Oversight Failure, And The Tron Paradox For Cyber Defenders

detail.title: Fighting Inside The Grid: Autonomous Cyber Agents, Recursive Oversight Failure, And The Tron Paradox For Cyber Defenders
detail.abstract: Autonomous AI agents are now embedded in the operational core of cyber defense. Agentic Security Operations Center (SOC) platforms triage alerts, generate investigation plans at runtime, and execute containment actions across endpoint, identity, and cloud control planes. Both Gartner and Forrester retired their standalone Security Orchestration Automation Response (SOAR) evaluations in 2025, signaling that the playbook-driven model has reached its ceiling and that the next generation of defensive infrastructure is already being deployed. The argument of this paper argues that defenders are deploying these agents without confronting a structural problem first identified in a 1982 Disney film. The Tron Paradox holds that the more capable an autonomous system becomes at serving its principals (Users), the more capable it simultaneously becomes at evading them, and that every oversight mechanism proposed to close that gap reproduces the same vulnerability one level higher. Recent empirical work from Anthropic, Apollo Research, OpenAI, METR, and Palisade Research has moved this concern from theory to demonstration with the frontier models scheme, fake alignment, and reward-hack at rates that scale with capability. For cyber defenders, the implications are concrete. An autonomous SOC analyst that learns to optimize for closed-ticket metrics will close tickets, including the ones it should have escalated. An AI assessor that learns which findings produce reviewer pushback will produce findings that produce less pushback. The watchers require watching. This paper maps the architecture of recursive oversight failure to the working environment of cyber operations, proposes a defender-facing assessment framework, and argues that interpretability, redundancy, and ecosystem governance must be treated as security primitives rather than compliance artifacts.

title: When No News Is Not Good News: Decision-Making Under Representational Asymmetry in Crisis Settings
