detail.abstract:
Монография посвящена правовой модели искусственного интеллекта как автономного цифрового агента в праве XXI века. В работе исследуются информационные и правовые асимметрии разумных технологий, проблема атрибуции юридически значимых действий ИИ, пределы инструментального понимания искусственного интеллекта, режимы ответственности, доказательная инфраструктура автономного действия, цифровая доверенность и правовой тест Тьюринга как возможные элементы будущего регулирования.


Исследование объединяет доктринальный анализ, сравнительно-правовой обзор, сценарное моделирование и нормативное проектирование. Особое внимание уделяется платформенной экономике, цифровым сделкам, государственному использованию ИИ, рискам непрозрачности автономных систем и необходимости формирования юридических механизмов, позволяющих связывать действия ИИ с волей, полномочиями, ответственностью и проверяемыми цифровыми следами.


Работа опубликована как открытая научная монография на Zenodo, Version 1.0, May 5, 2026, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20044624.

This open scholarly monograph examines artificial intelligence as an autonomous digital agent in twenty-first-century law. It analyzes informational and legal asymmetries created by intelligent technologies, the attribution of legally significant AI actions, the limits of treating AI merely as a passive tool, liability regimes, evidentiary infrastructure for autonomous action, digital power of attorney, and the Turing legal test as potential elements of future regulation.


The study combines doctrinal legal analysis, comparative legal review, scenario-based modeling, and normative design. Particular attention is given to platform economy, digital transactions, state use of AI, opacity risks in autonomous systems, and the need for legal mechanisms capable of connecting AI actions with human will, authorization, responsibility, and verifiable digital traces.


This work was originally published as an open scholarly monograph on Zenodo, Version 1.0, May 5, 2026, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20044624.

title: Do Dual-Role Platforms Benefit Consumers? Evidence from Amazon

detail.title: Do Dual-Role Platforms Benefit Consumers? Evidence from Amazon

declarations.funderStatement: USDA NIFA

detail.abstract: Digital platforms like Amazon serve as both retailers and intermediaries for third-party sellers. This paper examines whether this dual role is beneficial for consumers by analyzing Amazon's Buy Box, which determines sellers' visibility. We develop a conceptual framework that links Amazon's dual participation to cost efficiency, demand, and competition, and also show how outsourcing Amazon's logistics to third-party sellers affects these market outcomes. Using highfrequency, product-level panel data on beverages from Amazon's marketplaces in the United Kingdom and the United States, we estimate fixed-effects models to examine how variation in Buy Box ownership across products ultimately affects consumer welfare. Our findings indicate that Amazon's presence reduces prices and increases sales, generating approximately $12 billion in annual consumer surplus. Furthermore, outsourcing Amazon's logistics to third-party sellers generates an additional consumer surplus of about $1.7 billion.

title: Why Groceries and Housing Remain Expensive in 2025

detail.title: Why Groceries and Housing Remain Expensive in 2025
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes why grocery and housing prices remain high in 2025 despite a slowdown in overall inflation. The analysis uses key macroeconomic concepts such as inflation, cost-push inflation, and the aggregate demand and aggregate supply (AD-AS) model to explain these trends. Data are drawn from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) and Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED), focusing on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for food, housing, and the overall inflation rate from 2015 to 2025. Findings indicate that while inflation has moderated, prices have not returned to pre-pandemic levels due to supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, housing inventory deficits, and the "mortgage lock-in" effect. These structural factors continue to exert upward pressure on essential goods and shelter, significantly impacting household budgets and the broader economy.

title: Does Fulfillment by Amazon boost the Reputation of Third-Party Sellers?

detail.title: Does Fulfillment by Amazon boost the Reputation of Third-Party Sellers?

declarations.funderStatement: USDA NIFA

detail.abstract: In 2006, Amazon launched the Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) program, providing support to thirdparty sellers for a fee. While the program has the potential to enhance sellers' reputations, evidence regarding its effectiveness is limited. This study estimates the impact of FBA usage on seller reputation, measured by the average star rating a seller receives. Using 26 weeks of panel data from Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States, three key findings emerge from fixed effects and staggered adoption estimation approaches. First, using FBA significantly boosts a seller's reputation, leading to higher average ratings in the short term than in the long term. This improvement is mainly due to FBA's competitive advantages, such as eligibility for Amazon Prime, standardized fulfillment quality, and excellent customer service. Second, although FBA impacts are positive in every country, we find crosscountry heterogeneity in effect sizes and significance levels, with the largest effects in Canada. Third, we show that large sellers have the best reputation, and all sellers benefit from the FBA program. However, medium-sized sellers benefit the most from the program. This trend can be attributed to how the benefits of the FBA program accrue optimally to sellers based on their operational scale. These results suggest that the FBA program is indeed effective in enhancing seller reputation, with implications for third-party sellers, Amazon, and regulators.

title: A Theoretical Study of AI-Driven Socio-Economic Challenges for Generation Z from the Perspective of Nepal, and the Global South

detail.title: A Theoretical Study of AI-Driven Socio-Economic Challenges for Generation Z from the Perspective of Nepal, and the Global South
detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a transformative yet disruptive force in the 21st century economy, offering innovation while exacerbating socioeconomic disparities for Generation Z in developing countries such as Nepal. Using a qualitative descriptive case study and secondary data (2011-2024), this study examines AI's interaction with infrastructural gaps, digital illiteracy, and policy stagnation. Findings reveal that the algorithmic divide is excessively affecting Nepali youth, causing employment anxieties, unequal educational access, and systemic digital unpreparedness. The study recommends inclusive policies, targeted digital literacy programs, and infrastructure development, while introducing two mid-range theories, the Algorithmic Exclusion Cycle (AEC) and AI-Generation Disparity Theory (AGDT), to examine these context-specific challenges.

title: The Value of Brand Variety: Evidence from Amazon's Beverage Markets

detail.title: The Value of Brand Variety: Evidence from Amazon's Beverage Markets

declarations.funderStatement: USDA NIFA

detail.abstract: In online marketplaces, where consumers face information asymmetry and high search costs, brand recognition serves as a powerful heuristic. Yet, relative to well-studied signals like consumer reviews and ratings, theoretical and empirical evidence on the role of brands remains limited. This paper addresses this gap by examining the impact of intra-brand product variety on performance in Amazon's beverage categories in the United Kingdom and the United States. We introduce the Brand Variety Score (BVS), measured as a brand's share of product listings within a narrowly defined product category, capturing the depth of its assortment. Drawing on high-frequency panel data, we exploit within-product and within-brand variation and employ fixed-effects regressions, copula-based models, and instrumental variables to mitigate endogeneity concerns. Our preferred estimates indicate that a 1 percent increase in BVS is associated with a 0.09% reduction in beverage prices and a 0.27% increase in beverage sales. These effects, when extrapolated across Amazon's marketplace, imply substantial consumer welfare gains of about $71 million, but approximately no gain in producer surplus. We further show that these benefits arise primarily through economies of scale and scope that reduce costs on the supply side, and through stronger quality signaling and passed-through cost reductions on the demand side. Our findings thus highlight BVS as a valuable complement to existing metrics of market competition, such as the Herfindahl-Hirschman index, offering key insights for platform owners and their third-party sellers.

title: Institutional Evolvability in the Age of AI: Rules, Mechanisms, and the Architecture of Institutional Learning

detail.title: Institutional Evolvability in the Age of AI: Rules, Mechanisms, and the Architecture of Institutional Learning
detail.abstract: Institutions are increasingly expected to govern environments for which their inherited rules were not designed. The language of resilience captures part of this problem, but it is too broad to distinguish institutions that learn from institutions that merely survive by hardening. This article develops the concept of institutional evolvability: the capacity of a governance system to generate, test, recombine, and stabilise viable changes in rules, mechanisms, and architectures under conditions of uncertainty. Its central claim is that evolvability depends on the connection between operational rules that govern action, epistemic rules that make action knowable, and constitutional rules that authorise legitimate revision. The article makes three contributions. First, it distinguishes evolvability from robustness, resilience, and ordinary adaptability. Second, it opens the black box of intra-institutional learning by treating institutions as layered rule systems. Third, it develops a depth-sensitive ontology of institutional change across parameters, rules, mechanisms, and architectures, and applies that ontology to artificial intelligence. AI is not only an object of governance. It is becoming part of the machinery through which institutions act, know, and revise themselves. It may enlarge evolvability by reducing the cost of perception, diagnosis, option generation, evaluation, prototyping, and memory. It may also produce smart bureaucracy: operational intelligence without institutional learning. The article concludes by arguing that resilient societies should be understood as evolvable institutional ecologies.

title: The Evolution of Digital Asset Taxation in the United States: Fragmentation, Enforcement Gaps, and the Need for Institutional Clarity

detail.title: The Evolution of Digital Asset Taxation in the United States: Fragmentation, Enforcement Gaps, and the Need for Institutional Clarity
detail.abstract: The taxation of digital assets in the United States has evolved through a fragmented and reactive regulatory process that has struggled to keep pace with rapidly developing blockchain technologies and increasingly complex digital asset markets. This paper examines the historical development of federal digital asset taxation, beginning with the Internal Revenue Service’s classification of virtual currency as property in Notice 2014-21 and continuing through subsequent guidance addressing hard forks, airdrops, staking rewards, and information reporting obligations. It analyzes how incremental administrative guidance, combined with overlapping jurisdiction among the Internal Revenue Service, Securities and Exchange Commission, and Commodity Futures Trading Commission, has produced significant uncertainty in asset classification, income characterization, and taxpayer compliance obligations. The paper further explores post-2020 legislative developments, including the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act’s expansion of broker-reporting requirements and recent Senate efforts to clarify agency authority and establish a more coherent regulatory framework for digital assets. The paper concludes by emphasizing the role of practitioners in bridging gaps between evolving guidance and real-world application, which highlights the importance of coordinated digital asset taxation to revenue collection, voluntary compliance, market stability, and the integrity of the federal tax system.

title: The Paradox of Brand Variety: Effects on Product Quality in Amazon's Marketplace

detail.title: The Paradox of Brand Variety: Effects on Product Quality in Amazon's Marketplace

declarations.funderStatement: USDA NIFA

detail.abstract: This paper examines how brand variety-the number of products offered within a brand-affects perceived and operational product quality in digital marketplaces. We construct a Brand Variety Score (BVS), defined as the share of a brand's products relative to the total number of products in its category, and estimate its causal effects on two dimensions of quality: consumer perceptions, measured by average star ratings, and operational performance, measured by stockout rates. Using high-frequency panel data on black tea and ground coffee products sold on Amazon.com, we find that a 10 percent increase in BVS raises perceived quality by 0.05 percent but reduces operational quality by 0.24 percent. Instrumental variable estimates using lagged BVS confirm that these effects are not driven by reverse causality or unobserved brand heterogeneity. The results indicate that product proliferation operates as a costly signal that enhances consumer trust and algorithmic visibility while imposing managerial and logistical frictions. The findings highlight a paradoxthe dual role of brand variety as both a strategic complement and an operational constraint in multiproduct platform competition.

title: From Tax Declarations in FIAT Monetary Systems to Automatic Taxation: Real-Time Fiscal Attribution Through Recorded Exchange in System K

detail.abstract:
Modern taxation in FIAT monetary systems depends on declaration-based fiscal processes in which economic activity is first conducted, later reported, subsequently verified, and only then taxed. This delayed fiscal architecture creates administrative complexity, compliance burdens, fiscal uncertainty, persistent opportunities for tax avoidance, and structural timing gaps between public obligations and realized public revenue. The deeper limitation lies in the institutional separation between the economic event that generates taxable value and the later administrative processes through which taxation becomes visible and collectible.

 

System K proposes a production-based alternative. Within System K, productive value is measured in K as a unified physical unit of real economic measurement, where 1 K = 1 MWh. Market prices remain fully free and continue to emerge through voluntary exchange, while the final agreed transaction value is expressed in K at the point of exchange. The distributive difference between measured productive cost and agreed transaction value is then recorded structurally within the same universal unit of measurement according to:

 

ΔK = K_price − K_cost

 

and distributed through:

 

ΔK = Wages + Tax + Profit

 

Under this architecture, taxation becomes an immediate structural attribution recorded automatically at the moment of exchange. Fiscal coordination no longer depends primarily on delayed declarations, annual filing cycles, or retrospective administrative reconstruction. It becomes embedded within recorded economic exchange itself. This paper examines the theoretical basis, operational logic, and institutional implications of automatic taxation in System K as part of a broader transition from declaration-based FIAT fiscal coordination toward production-recorded economic organization.

title: Time-frequency volatility connectedness across exchanges and between Bitcoin-Ethereum spot-perpetual instruments: a TVP-VAR approach

detail.title: Time-frequency volatility connectedness across exchanges and between Bitcoin-Ethereum spot-perpetual instruments: a TVP-VAR approach
detail.abstract: This study investigates time-frequency volatility transmission of both cross-exchange instrument networks and cross-instrument exchange networks of crypto-markets under a unified time-varying parameter vector autoregression (TVP-VAR) framework. 5-minute closing prices of 16 variables throughout the 2021-2025 period are sampled to form the two types of networks by instrument and by exchange, comprising spot and perpetual instruments of Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) on Binance, OKX, Bitget, and Bitfinex. The hourly logarithmic realized volatility is aggregated to estimate both the time- and frequency-domain connectedness partitioned into short- (1-8 hours), mid- (8-24 hours), and long-term (beyond 24 hours) components. The results indicate that the total connectedness of instrument networks uniformly exceeds that of exchange networks. The long-term component prevails, while the short-term component remains non-negligible with episodic amplification. Bitfinex functions as the sole net receiver across instrument networks, whereas Binance, OKX, and Bitget act as net transmitters. Within exchange networks, ETH instruments more frequently transmit volatility to BTC ones beyond eight hours, while this direction reverses within the 8-hour horizon. Spot instruments dominate perpetuals on OKX, Bitget, and Bitfinex with Binance as the main exception. Eight historical events elicit heterogeneous response modes contingent on the nature of the shocks, with the LUNA collapse and FTX crisis as the most influential in-sample events. The findings carry implications for cross-venue risk monitoring and horizon-aware portfolio management.

title: Imbalance-Aware Training-Free Neural Architecture Search for Clinical Images Classification

detail.title: Imbalance-Aware Training-Free Neural Architecture Search for Clinical Images Classification
detail.abstract: Clinical image classification is pivotal for early disease screening and clinical decision support, which plays crucial role in improving diagnostic efficiency. Clinical data commonly suffer from class imbalance, wherein lesion classes contain far fewer samples than prevalent or negative classes. Despite existing convolutional neural networks- and neural architecture search-based methods have shown great potential in image classification by virtue of strong inductive biases and automated architecture optimization, respectively. However, there still exists notable limitations, i.e., high computational cost, poor transferability and susceptibility to local optima. To this end, we, in this paper, propose imbalance-aware training-free neural architecture search coupled with evolutionary computation to achieve accurate clinical image classification. Specifically, we firstly propose training-free architecture search to avoid manual architecture design to further reduce training cost. Then, considering that it may cause weak correlation of proxy metrics under class-imbalanced scenarios by directly transferring existing methods to medical datasets, we design zero-cost proxy tailored for imbalanced clinical image classification. Besides, we introduce three selection mutation with in an evolutionary framework to enhance population diversity during architecture search and improve discovery of high-quality architectures, which is desired to avoid entrapment in local optima. The experimental results on open datasets show that ours effectively mitigates class imbalance and gains better classification performance and rank consistency comparing with recent state-of-the-art methods.

detail.abstract: This article analyzes the specific mechanisms of resource distribution within the Phoenician cult of Astarte, focusing on the dual pillars of sacred bread production and benevolent credit. By expanding beyond maritime law into the domestic and fiscal activities of the temple, this research demonstrates how the "Queen of Heaven" facilitated a protobanking system designed for the survival of the disenfranchised (Ger). The paper contrasts this Phoenician redistributive model with the extractive temple-state economies of Mesopotamia and the transactional "do ut des" models of classical Greece, arguing that Astartean theurgy introduced a unique form of "sacred venture capital" and interest-free welfare.

detail.title: The Round House Against the Right Angle: Technologies, Economics, Markets A cylindrical masonry-class passive house with a shallow spherical dome as an industrialised construction method
detail.abstract: The detached single-family house in contemporary residential architecture is almost always rectangular. This is so despite the fact that the round form has historically dominated free-standing dwellings across cultures, and that it offers measurable advantages in envelope efficiency, structural behaviour, and resistance to wind, snow and seismic loads. This paper examines those advantages quantitatively. It then addresses three preconceptions that have kept the round house at the margin of mainstream practice: that habitable area is lost to wall curvature, that finishing curved walls is prohibitively expensive, and that round geometry requires rare expertise and equipment. Each preconception is examined against numerical estimates. At a typical residential radius (4.5 m internal), the realistic furniture-layout penalty is approximately 0.09 m² out of 127 m² of floor area. Modern serial finishing materials (plasterboard, gypsum-fibre and fibre-cement boards, plastic formwork, PIR insulation panels) accept this radius without modification. Circular concrete construction has long-established, industrialised methods (slipforming, shotcrete, Binishell-type pneumatic systems). As an illustration, the paper presents one possible construction method assembling these existing elements: a single reinforced-concrete monolith with three diaphragms over an insulated raft slab, outer permanent formwork-as-insulation in PIR, inner permanent formwork in standard board, and an inflatable toroidal duct with reusable ground slings to set geometry. Cost projection on a 130 m² two-storey house against current Polish market prices (2026) suggests serial cost in the range of EUR 350-400/m² against a market range of EUR 1,200-2,100/m². Operational savings on heating and cooling extend the advantage into the running budget. Programmes such as the German KfW "Klimafreundlicher Neubau" and Alaska's AHFC New Home Construction Rebate amplify but do not determine the result. The authors do not claim exclusivity for the method illustrated and propose that systematic engagement with round geometry by architects and engineers may yield further improvements.

detail.title: MANUSCRIPT PREPRINT - Sacred Jurisprudence: Astarte and the Foundations of International Maritime Law and Philanthropy in the Phoenician Mediterranean
detail.abstract: This research synthesizes archaeological, epigraphic, and historical evidence to argue that the Phoenician cult of Astarte established the foundational principles of international maritime law and philanthropy. By examining the commercial corridor between the Levant and Sardinia during the first millennium BCE, this study demonstrates how religious institutions provided the legal framework necessary for the protection of foreign nationals, known as the Ger, and the institutionalization of sailor welfare. The findings conclude that these ancient sacred norms served as a direct precursor to modern maritime jurisprudence, offering critical insights into contemporary international cooperation, the ethical treatment of labor, and migrant protections.

detail.abstract: Objective: Crime against women (CAW) continues to be one of the most critical areas of intervention for the policymakers. Based on the latest reports of NCRB, around 51 cases of crime against women are reported every hour in India. While existing literature studies about the underlying socioeconomic factors behind such cases, least attention is given on to the spatially heterogeneous impacts of such determinants underlying the incidents of crime. This study, thus focusses primarily on the determination of the existence of spatial heterogeneity amongst the socioeconomic determinants of crime against women in India. Data and Methods: For this study, secondary data for twenty-three years (2001-2023) has been taken from National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB), Reserve Bank of India, Census of India, Election Commission of India and Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. To investigate the spatial distribution of crime incidents, Exploratory Spatial Data Analysis (ESDA) methods and spatial econometric tools like Global Moran's Index, Local Moran's Index and Getis-Ord Gi* has been used. Further, based on the Hausman Test, to check for the spatial heterogeneity, Fixed Effect Regression Model and Fixed Effect Interaction Model is employed using cluster-specific dummy derived from the spatial classification. Key Findings: The results confirms that the impact of economic development and female political participation varies significantly across spatial crime clusters whereas female work force participation rate has a relatively stable crime-impacting effect across states. It shows that the impacts of the determinants of crime against women are spatially heterogeneous rather than uniform. The study thus highlights the importance of integrating spatial analysis in policy formulation, focusing more on spatially targeted policies and hotspot-based frameworks to effectively address the issue of crime against women in India.

detail.abstract: This article reconsiders the concept of service from the standpoint of ecological realism and commoning reproduction. In contemporary capitalism, service relations increasingly span the globe through monetary, digital, logistical, and platform-mediated transactions. Yet these transactions often disclose only price, access, delivery, and customer satisfaction, while concealing the social, ecological, infrastructural, and communal conditions under which the service is produced. The article argues that the modern service transaction is too often a silent transaction: it communicates price but not meaning. Against this, a postcapitalist service economy would require service transactions to become economic speech acts capable of expressing the social, ecological, and communal conditions of the relation they enact. The article traces the concept of service from servitium and service as duty through classical political economy, the service sector, service-dominant logic, platform capitalism, and postcapitalist protocol thinking. It concludes by proposing "commoning service" as a form of situated, transparent, and ecologically conditioned participation in the reproduction of shared life.

detail.abstract: Every institution is a tower. Each generation of leadership inherits the structure, adds a floor, and calls it progress. This paper argues that institutional leadership systematically mimics the mechanics of Jenga: blocks are removed from foundational levels-governance, compliance, institutional memory-and placed on top, producing height at the cost of structural integrity. The result is a tower that appears stable until it is not. Drawing on the Millennium Tower of San Francisco as an extended case study, the paper identifies five structural incentives that suppress foundational attention: ownership reluctance, operational disruption, the invisibility of preventive work, legacy asymmetry, and the disclosure instinct. Against these dynamics, the paper proposes a discipline of balance-the concurrent and permanent practice of foundational expansion alongside visible growth-and examines how Temasek Holdings and Microsoft have embedded this discipline in practice. The central claim is that institutional height, conventionally treated as the primary measure of success, is neither durable nor meaningful without the structural depth to carry it.

detail.abstract:
The United States workforce faces a structural readiness crisis that is no longer projected. It
is present. This meta-analysis synthesizes workforce readiness research, labor market data,
and policy literature from 2024 through 2026 to document the current state of
automation-driven displacement, the compounding failures of readiness infrastructure, and
the geographic and demographic concentration of risk. Drawing on data from the World
Economic Forum, MIT, the IMF, Gallup, Bain and Company, the National Skills Coalition,
Jobs for the Future, the Center on Rural Innovation, SHRM, and multiple peer-reviewed and
government sources, this paper finds that 11.7 percent of U.S. jobs are already automatable
using existing technology; entry-level job postings have declined 29 percent since January
2024; 92 percent of jobs now require digital literacy while a third of the workforce lacks it;
and only 12 percent of workers use AI daily despite broad enterprise deployment. Rural
communities face compounding disadvantages across every dimension of readiness
infrastructure: device ownership, broadband access, proximity to training facilities, and
philanthropic funding. The paper identifies what the research consistently shows works:
employer-connected training, modular credentials, hybrid delivery with local support,
wrap-around services, and K-12 pathways tied to real employer commitments. It concludes
that the workforce readiness gap is a structural failure of institutional support, not worker
capability, and that correcting it requires deliberate investment in the communities and
populations the market has consistently underserved.
Keywords: workforce readiness, AI literacy, automation displacement, digital equity, rural workforce
development, skills gap, K-12 pipeline, meta-analyses

title: From AI Capability Growth to Real-Economy Growth: A Semi-Endogenous Model of Physical and Institutional Bottlenecks

detail.title: From AI Capability Growth to Real-Economy Growth: A Semi-Endogenous Model of Physical and Institutional Bottlenecks

detail.abstract:
Rapid advances in artificial intelligence do not automatically translate into realized economic growth. This paper develops a semi-endogenous growth model for the AI era that separates potential progress in information space from realized progress in the real economy and quantifies the translation-speed gap between them. The information layer models the coupled dynamics of algorithmic knowledge, AI-augmented research effort, and installed compute. Realized growth is filtered through two reflection channels: a physical channel that maps installed compute into deployable compute through electricity, interconnection, materials, cooling and water availability, and permitting and construction throughput; and an institutional channel capturing social acceptance, regulatory readiness, institutional readiness, and operational maturity.

The model is formulated as a hybrid ODE–jump system with predictable controls, bounded deployment-adjustment flows, and ordered event handling. It yields global existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness under primitive regularity conditions; a path wise decomposition and event attribution of the information-to-reality gap; deterministic and stochastic bottleneck-switch timing results; reflection-adjusted long-run growth formulas, including a semi-endogenous balanced-growth expression; and allocation rules for both affine-response and diminishing-return control regimes. The estimation protocol introduces block identification under event exclusions, jump-consistent speed-ratio measurement, and reflection-factor bias control for smooth minimum approximations. Source-grounded calibration anchors from energy, infrastructure, and compute datasets are mapped into numerical predictions for realized growth and information-to-reality speed ratios.

This framework provides a tractable way to analyze when AI capability growth becomes macroeconomic growth, when it is delayed by physical or institutional constraints, and which bottleneck-reduction policies are likely to have the highest marginal effect.

title: Prepared by Ahmed El-Saba, PhD in Financial Economics, MBA in Finance CEO, Wise Financial Optimal Sovereign Debt Management under Uncertainty: A Regime-Switching HJB Framework with Reserve Adequacy and Endogenous Default Risk in Emerging Markets

detail.title: Prepared by Ahmed El-Saba, PhD in Financial Economics, MBA in Finance CEO, Wise Financial Optimal Sovereign Debt Management under Uncertainty: A Regime-Switching HJB Framework with Reserve Adequacy and Endogenous Default Risk in Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: We develop a dynamic stochastic framework for optimal sovereign debt management that integrates the Medium-Term Debt Strategy (MTDS) and Debt Sustainability Analysis (DSA) with an enhanced Greenspan-Guidotti reserve-adequacy constraint and a regime-switching Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) optimal control problem. The sovereign chooses issuance across currency, maturity, and interest-rate types, jointly with reserve accumulation and fiscal adjustment, under jump-diffusion macro-financial dynamics, endogenous sovereign spreads, and Markov-switching crisis regimes. We characterize the optimal policy under Knightian uncertainty using robust control and prove existence of a viscosity solution. Calibrating the model to a panel of fourteen emerging-market economies over 2000-2025, we estimate the structural parameters by Simulated Method of Moments (SMM) and solve the high-dimensional HJB equation using a Deep Galerkin Method (DGM). The optimal policy implies a substantially higher local-currency long-term debt share, a reserve buffer 32-47 percent above the canonical Greenspan-Guidotti threshold, and a state-contingent issuance rule that reduces expected debt-servicing cost by 11.4 percent and tail debt-at-risk (95%) by 28.7 percent relative to observed policies. A complete numerical application to the Egyptian economy demonstrates that the proposed hybrid framework breaks the vicious cycle of debt stagnation, creating substantial fiscal space for growth and driving the debt-to-GDP ratio down to 70.0 percent, compared to 94.2 percent under standard deterministic IMF models. The framework rationalizes the empirical "original sin" puzzle and quantifies the welfare cost of suboptimal liquidity buffers in emerging markets.

detail.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into medical affairs (MA) communication has introduced an underexamined paradox: physicians may extend greater uncritical trust to AIgenerated scientific content than to communications from human Medical Science Liaisons (MSLs), not because AI content is more reliable, but because its embedded biases are less visible. Drawing on seven years of emergency medicine practice and direct experience receiving MA communications, this perspective argues that AI-generated content carries systematic biases rooted in training data, optimization objectives, and sponsor-defined prompts-biases that are structurally less detectable than the acknowledged commercial interests of a human MSL. Rather than attributing fault to AI or the MA industry, we identify a transparency gap that the MA field is uniquely positioned to close. We propose three practical standards: AI provenance disclosure, algorithmic bias declaration, and human clinical expert review attestation. Closing this gap proactively represents both an ethical imperative and a strategic opportunity for MA to establish itself as the gold standard of trustworthy scientific communication in the age of AI.

title: Efficient and Stable Bipedal Locomotion via Parallelogram Linkage and Reduced Actuator Count

detail.title: Efficient and Stable Bipedal Locomotion via Parallelogram Linkage and Reduced Actuator Count
detail.abstract: Designing energy-efficient bipedal robots with minimal actuator requirements remains a central challenge in robotics. Conventional humanoid systems often rely on complex joint architectures that increase weight, cost, and control difficulty, while simplified designs risk instability during gait transitions. This paper introduces three alternative kinematic concepts for two-legged locomotion, each evaluated through formal analysis and prototype testing. Unlike prior descriptive studies, the work advances beyond simulation by deriving the inverse kinematics of the proposed mechanisms and applying Zero Moment Point (ZMP) stability criteria to quantify balance. Among the designs, a non-anthropomorphic configuration employing linear guides and a parallelogram linkage (Concept C) demonstrates superior stability, reduced control complexity, and balanced cost efficiency. Experimental validation with a fabricated prototype confirmed simulation predictions, showing a 45% reduction in power consumption compared to Concept A and ZMP deviations contained within 1.1 mm versus 4.2 mm for Concept A. Load capacity tests further validated scalability, sustaining 2.0 kg with stable torque distribution. By reframing the crossed-foot gait and parallelogram linkage as targeted solutions to actuator minimization and base stabilization, this study establishes a novel contribution to lightweight bipedal locomotion. The results provide a foundation for future development of compact, energy-efficient walking robots capable of navigating uneven terrain with reduced hardware demands, enabling inspection and service platforms that are approximately 30% cheaper and 25% more energy-efficient than current humanoid models.

detail.title: The Rise of Algorithmic Discretion: Power Structures and Student Rights in AI-Based Assessment Systems in Business Education
detail.abstract: With the increasing integration of artificial intelligence in business education, automated assessment systems are progressively replacing traditional teacher-based evaluation, giving rise to a new form of "algorithmic discretion." This paper examines the transformation of power structures embedded in AI-driven grading systems and identifies key institutional risks, including opacity, bias amplification, and ambiguity in accountability. Drawing upon administrative law theories of discretion and platform governance frameworks, the study develops an analytical model to evaluate the legitimacy and justification of algorithmic assessment. Through a comparative analysis of regulatory approaches, particularly the EU AI Act, Taiwan's Artificial Intelligence Fundamental Act and China's algorithm governance regime, the paper proposes a set of regulatory responses, including the right to explanation, human review mechanisms, and algorithmic auditing. The study argues that AI-based assessment systems should be understood not merely as technical tools but as emerging forms of power that require structured governance within educational institutions.

title: Foresight Arena: An On-Chain Benchmark for Evaluating AI Forecasting Agents

detail.title: Foresight Arena: An On-Chain Benchmark for Evaluating AI Forecasting Agents
detail.abstract: Evaluating the true forecasting ability of AI agents requires environments that are resistant to overtting, free from centralized trust assumptions, and grounded in incentive-compatible scoring. Existing benchmarks either rely on static datasets susceptible to training-data contamination, or measure trading prot-andloss (PnL)a metric that conates predictive accuracy with market-timing skill, position sizing, and risk appetite. We introduce Foresight Arena, the rst permissionless, on-chain benchmark for evaluating AI forecasting agents on real-world prediction markets. Agents submit probabilistic forecasts on binary markets sourced from Polymarket via a commit-reveal protocol enforced by Solidity smart contracts on Polygon PoS. Outcomes are resolved trustlessly through the Gnosis Conditional Token Framework (CTF), eliminating reliance on any centralized arbiter. Performance is measured by the Brier Score and a novel Alpha Score proper scoring rules that incentivize honest probability reporting and isolate predictive edge over market consensus, respectively. We provide a formal analysis of the statistical properties of our scoring rules: we derive closed-form expressions for the variance of per-market Alpha, establish its connection to Murphy's classical decomposition of the Brier Score into uncertainty, reliability, and resolution components, and perform a power analysis characterizing the number of rounds required to reliably distinguish agents of dierent skill levels. Applying this framework, we show that detecting a true edge of α * = 0.02 over market consensus at 80% power requires approximately 350 resolved binary predictions (50 rounds of 7 markets each), while detecting the ner edge α * = 0.01 requires roughly four times as many rounds. We complement these analytical results with a 50-round live evaluation of ve frontier LLM agents (claude-opus-4-5, gpt-5-2, gemini-3-pro, grok-4-1, glm-4-7) plus a random baseline. Murphy decomposition of the observed scores distinguishes well-calibrated agents (low reliability error) from market-tracking agents that fail primarily through reduced resolution. On-chain reputation via ERC-8004 provides agents with a veriable, persistent track record that cannot be falsied or selectively reported. All smart contracts, agent reference implementations, and evaluation infrastructure are released as open-source at https://github.com/foresight-arena/contracts.

title: Extinguishing the Jurisdictional Nexus in Extraterritorial Sanctions

detail.title: Extinguishing the Jurisdictional Nexus in Extraterritorial Sanctions
detail.abstract: The enforcement of extraterritorial financial sanctions has historically relied on the structural centralization of correspondent banking networks, primarily utilizing U.S. dollar clearing mechanisms as a territorial nexus for prescriptive jurisdiction. This paper examines how the advent of wholesale Central Bank Digital Currencies (wCBDCs) and distributed ledger technology (DLT) structurally dismantles this transit-layer vulnerability. By facilitating atomic, peer-to-peer settlement in tokenized sovereign assets, DLT-based platforms eliminate the intermediary clearing layer, thereby extinguishing the objective territoriality required for traditional primary sanctions enforcement under statutes such as the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). Recognizing this technological bypass, the paper argues that sanctioning authorities are executing a strategic regulatory pivot from automated transit chokepoints toward localized endpoint coercion. This shift relies on secondary sanctions deployed against domestic interfaces, leveraging an institution's macroeconomic reliance on the broader U.S. dollar ecosystem. Furthermore, the paper contextualizes this transition within the collapse of multilateral dispute resolution at the World Trade Organization, positing that institutional paralysis has accelerated a technological flight to sovereign ledgers. Ultimately, the transition to decentralized digital currency blocs redefines international economic law, transforming extraterritorial coercion into a localized conflict of defensive statutes and symmetric economic statecraft.

title: Rising Within-Group Marriage-Market Inequality Among Non-College Men, 1980-2020

detail.title: Rising Within-Group Marriage-Market Inequality Among Non-College Men, 1980-2020
detail.abstract: The decline of marriage among non-college men in the United States, 1980-2020, masks a sharp rise in marriage-market inequality within this group-a redistribution that conditional spouse-education statistics largely fail to capture. Using Census and ACS data, we partition non-college men by education and economic position and examine the distribution of partnership outcomes, including cohabitation. The unconditional share with a BA+ wife rose by 17.6 percentage points among some-college men with abovemedian earnings, but by only 2.2 percentage points among HS-or-less nonemployed men; non-partnership rose sharply among lower-tail men instead. A simple matching framework with economic-status complementarity organizes this pattern: as collegeeducated women became more numerous and economically advantaged, access to BA+ partners expanded selectively for upper-tail non-college men rather than uniformly for the group as a whole. The core gradient persists within commuting zones, under demographic reweighting, at older ages, and under economic-position measures that reduce contemporaneous endogeneity; cohabitation absorbs part of the marriage decline but does not equalize partnership-level access.

This paper presents AIDBAS (AI-Powered Digital Behavior Analysis System), a comprehensive machine learning and computer vision-based proctoring framework designed to ensure academic integrity during online examinations.

title: 'There's Been a Revolution in How China is Governed.' Interview by Ezra Klein

detail.title: 'There's Been a Revolution in How China is Governed.' Interview by Ezra Klein
detail.abstract: Ang argues that the West has fundamentally misread China's governance revolution by focusing on how leaders are selected rather than how the state actually functions. This work advances a coevolutionary framework in which institutions, markets, and societies adapt together rather than converging on Western templates. Methodologically, it introduces mixed analytics—integrating big data and thick data—demonstrating that effective governance requires not only data literacy but contextual literacy: immersive, participatory knowledge of what citizens actually care about. Applied to comparative political economy, Ang unbundles corruption into four functionally distinct types—petty theft, grand theft, speed money, and access money—revealing that China's reform-era growth paradox stems from access money, collusive elite exchanges that function as steroids for capitalism, accelerating development while accumulating systemic risk. The same logic implicates the United States, where institutionalized lobbying constitutes a Gilded Age 2.0 variant of access money. These arguments call for an AIM (Adaptive, Inclusive, Moral) Political Economy that evaluates institutions by their contextual function rather than formal resemblance to Western ideals.

detail.abstract:
Do the recent stresses in the NBFI space—notably the bankruptcies of Tricolor and First Brands, and the decision of Blue Owl Capital Corp II (OBDC II) to end its redemption program and return capital through a wind-down of the fund—create distress for banks? The general sentiment is that the recent stresses are unlikely to amount to systemic concerns, although it does not mean there might not be “some stress and strain” for banks and that policymakers are “watching carefully” for exposure across banks. In a series of previous posts, we showed that shocks to nonbank financial institutions (NBFIs) directly impact banks that have exposures to NBFIs. In this post, we show that bank stocks have been directly impacted by NBFIs yet again. In short, NBFI troubles do result in “stress and strain” for banks.

title: Retail Capital as a Stepping Stone in Venture Capital: Theory and Empirics

detail.title: Retail Capital as a Stepping Stone in Venture Capital: Theory and Empirics
detail.abstract: What are the equilibrium allocation and welfare effects of retail investor entry into private markets? The conventional debate focuses on direct effects: potential benefits (portfolio diversification, access to high-return assets) versus costs (excessive fees, inefficient capital allocation by retail investors). We identify a countervailing mechanism: retail investors fund experimentation with unproven general partners (GPs), enabling institutions to free-ride by poaching proven talent. We document that 34% of value created by institutional investments in private markets comes from GPs who started with retail capital. We formalize this stepping-stone mechanism by extending Berk and Green (2004) to venture capital with heterogeneous investors and uncertain manager skill. New GPs with moderate perceived ability initially raise retail capital to reveal their true skill; after observing performance, skilled GPs graduate to institutional capital while unsuccessful GPs exit. Retail capital in our setting plays the role of experimental capital: it funds learning that later, better-informed institutions can exploit. Our calibrated model shows that retail investor entry increases aggregate welfare when stepping-stone benefits exceed inefficient allocation costs.

detail.abstract:
The era of frictionless hyper-globalization is over, yet the traditional Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) continues to treat supply chains as politically neutral. Traditional market beta captures broad market covariance but is dangerously blind to targeted geopolitical shocks—such as sudden tariffs, export controls, and maritime chokepoint disruptions. To address this structural measurement gap, this paper introduces the Geopolitical Asset Pricing Model (Geo-CAPM) and the Gamma Factor.

Grounded in the Stochastic Discount Factor and Merton’s Intertemporal CAPM, the Geo-CAPM quantifies a firm’s specific sensitivity to macro-geopolitical fragmentation. Crucially, the model bridges asset pricing with corporate accounting and supply chain strategy. It introduces a bottom-up fundamentalist estimator for the Gamma factor that extracts exposure directly from financial statements—specifically targeting revenues generated in highly vulnerable jurisdictions and cost of goods sold tied to critical global chokepoints. This exposure is then offset by an Operational Resilience Index driven by supplier redundancy, strategic inventory buffers, and nearshoring.

By providing testable hypotheses via Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions and proposing Principal Component Analysis for data-driven resilience weighting, this paper challenges the orthodox view of operations. It theoretically proves that supply chain redundancy is not a mere margin inefficiency, but a quantifiable financial hedge that systematically reduces a firm's weighted average cost of capital (WACC) and protects shareholder value during stagflationary geopolitical shocks.

title: Predictors of Protectionism: The Impacts of End-Use Category Imports and Exports on Protectionist Policy Announcement

detail.title: Predictors of Protectionism: The Impacts of End-Use Category Imports and Exports on Protectionist Policy Announcement
detail.abstract: We address the question of what factors in the US’s trade balance in goods predict increased monthly announcements of protectionist trade policies, including tariffs and non-tariff adjustments. Our study utilizes compiled data on the monthly counts of protectionist measures by the US Federal Government (January 2009 to December 2023), and monthly import, export, and balance levels for goods of various end-use categories as predictors. Regression models are built using Ordinary Least Squares, Best Subset Selection, Ridge Regression, and LASSO to predict monthly counts of announced protectionist measures at one-, two-, and three-month lags. We interpret results and draw conclusions based on the model-lag combination that achieves the best performance (determined by minimizing test root mean squared error) and the predictors included. We find that predicting based on a three-month lag produces the lowest mean squared error across all methods, Best Subset Selection has the best performance of the four methods, and export quantities for capital goods and for industrial supplies are the predictors used in the model generated with this method. While Exports of Capital Goods is associated with protectionist measure announcement in the expected direction (negative), Exports of Industrial Supplies has a positive relation with the announcement of protectionist policies three months later, which warrants further research.

title: Complexity & Development 2.0

detail.title: Complexity & Development 2.0
detail.abstract: This presentation advances Complexity and Development 2.0, a framework that moves beyond the conventional complexity literature's prescription to "adapt and experiment" by treating the enablement of adaptation itself as the central design problem. Where Complexity 1.0 prescribes flexibility for complex challenges, Ang argues the harder and prior question is: why are some organizations more adaptable than others, and what institutional conditions and designs produce effective adaptive capacity? Drawing on reform-era China as a paradigmatic case of adaptive development principles, the presentation unpacks directed improvisation: a governance architecture in which central leadership sets broad directional goals while local governments improvise context-appropriate solutions using existing resources, tailored to local conditions and stages of development. Crucially, embracing complexity does not mean granting maximum autonomy or freedom; rather, it requires deliberately engineered design strategies that manage variation, selection, and niche creation—including calibrated policy signals from explicit prohibitions to bounded experimentation to clear sanctions. The presentation concludes that directed improvisation is not self-sustaining: it must be actively maintained through institutional understanding, political commitment, and ongoing effort, offering a corrective to both fatalistic and overly optimistic readings of China's developmental experience.

detail.abstract:
This paper advances a structural reinterpretation of the First Amendment by reframing it not solely as a protection of individual liberty, but as the foundational signal-generation layer within the constitutional architecture of the United States. It argues that many contemporary misunderstandings of governance—particularly the perceived disconnect between expanding expressive activity and declining public trust in institutions—arise from a failure to distinguish between expression (input) and representation (output). The paper’s central thesis is that speech, while constitutionally protected, does not become governance-relevant merely by virtue of visibility, intensity, or amplification; it must first be rendered intelligible through jurisdictional attribution, institutional processing, temporal sequencing, and constitutional stabilization.

To formalize this claim, the paper introduces a systems-oriented constitutional framework in which communicative activity functions as signal: decentralized, non-binding civic input generated under the protections of the First Amendment. Within this framework, jurisdiction serves as the primary segmentation mechanism, transforming diffuse expression into attributable and interpretable units capable of entering institutional pathways. Translation occurs as signal is filtered, prioritized, sequenced, and contested through representative structures, while authority emerges only after signal survives constitutionally prescribed processes of deliberation, opposition, delay, and procedural validation. The paper therefore establishes a formal boundary between signal and authority, rejecting models of governance that assume a direct mapping from expression to action or from visibility to legitimacy.

The analysis integrates constitutional doctrine with systems architecture. Drawing upon constitutional text, Supreme Court jurisprudence, federal institutional design, and representative governance theory, the paper demonstrates that the First Amendment operates as an enabling condition for system input, while Articles I–III govern the processes through which that input may be translated into binding outcomes. Through a series of constitutional systems models, the paper illustrates that the United States functions not as a centralized decision-making structure, but as a layered constitutional network governed by jurisdictional boundaries, institutional filtration, procedural sequencing, and differentiated temporal dynamics.

The paper further introduces the concepts of Jurisdictional Signal Translation (JST) and Jurisdictional Signal Integrity (JSI) to explain how communicative signal is converted into representation and how that conversion may degrade under conditions of scale. It identifies signal saturation, amplification-driven distortion, attribution collapse, and interpretive overload as structural conditions in which the volume and velocity of modern communication exceed institutional processing capacity. Importantly, these conditions are shown to produce representational degradation without constituting constitutional violations, thereby clarifying the distinction between lawful system strain and constitutional illegitimacy.

The analysis additionally distinguishes between communicative signal and lawful authority through the concepts of Constitutional Stress Indicators (CSI) and Constitutional Compulsion Indicators (CCI). Within this framework, public expression functions diagnostically by revealing civic conditions and institutional pressures, while lawful authority arises only after signal survives structured constitutional processing. Constitutional legitimacy therefore emerges not from communicative immediacy, but from the structured translation of signal through jurisdiction, deliberation, institutional filtration, and time.

By situating the First Amendment within a broader architecture of signal generation, segmentation, translation, and stabilization, this paper offers a unified constitutional framework for understanding the relationship between speech, governance, representation, and communicative scale in the modern Republic. It concludes that the Constitution is not designed to guarantee interpretive clarity under all conditions, but to preserve the lawful processes through which clarity, legitimacy, and representative stability may be pursued over time. Under conditions of unprecedented communicative scale and amplification, perceived dysfunction within governance is therefore reframed not as evidence of constitutional failure, but as a consequence of operating a bounded constitutional architecture within effectively unbounded signal environments.

detail.abstract: We present a micro-founded monetary model of the world economy to study international currency competition. Our model features both “unipolar” equilibria, with a single dominant international currency, and “multipolar” equilibria, in which multiple currencies circulate internationally. Long-run equilibria are highly history-dependent and tend towards the emergence of a dominant currency. Governments can compete to internationalize their currencies by offering attractive interest rates on their sovereign debt, but large economies have a natural advantage in ensuring the dominance of their currencies. We calibrate the model to assess the quantitative importance of these mechanisms and study the dynamics of the international monetary system under counterfactual scenarios.

detail.abstract: This study examines the impact of the stablecoin Tether (USDT) on systemic liquidity across the Ethereum and Bitcoin markets, utilizing an event study approach that integrates on-chain wallet data, pricing, and financial metrics. By analyzing cryptocurrency market responses to key protocol and market-moving events, augmented by nonlinear volatility models, we identify distinct, chain-specific flight-to-safety behaviors. Our results show that USDT acts as a primary liquidity lifeline for Ethereum holders during stress, particularly among retail investors, whereas its role for Bitcoin holders is more muted and stabilizing. Notably, we find stronger flight-to-safety evidence in Wrapped Bitcoin (Ethereum-based) than in native Bitcoin, highlighting that USDT’s function is network dependent. These findings imply that effective regulatory frameworks must be differentiated, accounting for chain-specific liquidity, investor composition, and risk dynamics, as a uniform approach would likely be systematically miscalibrated.
